543664|2026-03.headline: Kaynes FY26 revenue rose 33.2% to INR3,626 crore, but missed the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance, with operating cash flow of about INR600 crore negative.
543664|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the revenue shortfall to West Asia-related customer deferments, supply chain delays and one large EV two-wheeler customer cutting volumes by about 90%. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was INR5,741 million (15.8% margin) and PAT INR3,639 million (10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR12,426 million (+26% YoY) and PAT of INR912 million. Cash flow weakened sharply, driven by the smart metering subsidiary (Iskraemeco) with receivables of about INR1,365 crore, while the standalone EMS business turned cash positive. Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue number and instead guided to outgrowing the market at roughly twice the market growth rate.

financial_highlights.change: PBT hit by about INR32 crore of quarterly intangible amortisation
from 83 days FY24; management also cited 64 to 54 days

segments.name: EMS (standalone/KEMPL)
segments.commentary: FY26 EMS revenue about INR2,655 crore (Q1 INR442 crore, Q2 INR683 crore, Q3 INR667 crore, Q4 INR862 crore), growing about 26-30%. Standalone EMS operating cash flow INR250 crore positive versus INR65 crore last year; EMS receivables INR399 crore at year end versus INR379 crore at start.

segments.name: Smart metering (Iskraemeco subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR971 crore (roughly 24-25% of group revenue), with receivables about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current. Installation delays in rural areas and state-government/DISCOM payment cycles are holding up collections; securitisation has discounted only about INR40 crore so far.

segments.name: OSAT
segments.commentary: Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27. Management cites revenue visibility above INR25,000 million over five years. Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister; FY27 production estimate INR250-300 crore, export-oriented.

segments.name: PCB
segments.commentary: Management sees a confirmed demand pipeline for five years with customers seeking more capacity. FY27 production estimate INR300-400 crore; first year of operation.

segments.name: Rail (Kavach)
segments.commentary: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; approvals expected in H1 FY27, with bulk orders in H2. Management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

segments.name: EV / automotive
segments.commentary: EV segment grew about 28% in FY26 despite the large two-wheeler customer falling about 90%. Company is moving from PCB supply into assemblies and products.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 revenue number; management guides to growing at about twice the market rate (market cited at 15-18% EMS growth), with quarterly updates on market versus Kaynes growth.
Standalone EMS to stay cash positive, with working capital days improving by about 8-10 days in the coming years.
Consolidated operating cash flow: management expects the INR600 crore negative to fall by 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end.
Metering receivables and installation expected to be completed within about 3 quarters; the business will move to an EMS-component-only model for new orders.
Target of NPD-led and value-added revenue at nearly 30% of total revenue over the coming years.
Smart meter FY27 revenue expected roughly flat to slightly up or down versus INR971 crore, with about 50% of volume on the old model and about 50% on the new model.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles (Iskraemeco and August Electronics, about INR320 crore) going forward, after the Q4 catch-up of about INR32 crore.
capex_capacity: OSAT Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27 (Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister).
FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore, mainly from acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics (Canada, North America EMS), with about INR320 crore capitalised.
Mysore facility crossed INR10,000 million revenue in FY26.
Metering: about 35 lakh meters on current order, plus a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension; 2-3 months needed to complete pending supply, with installation taking 1-2 quarters more.
Launched three products now in production (SOP started), and a 9-month product launch cycle versus 12-18 months previously.
Investing in NPD engineering, co-development, digital and R&D infrastructure, and predictive maintenance / Industry 4.0 at 2 plants.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR9,000 crore, described as diversified and non-cancellable; management says there is no structural deterioration in demand.
Q4 and FY26 shortfall attributed to West Asia conflict, last-minute customer deferments, supply chain delays and product timing shifts; some revenue recognition shifted though orders remain valid.
Auto industry outlook cut from mid-double-digit growth (December projection) to single-digit or low double-digit, per management, which raised caution on offtake.
Aerospace, railway, defence, space and EV are being added to reduce dependence on any one vertical.
OSAT and PCB output expected to be export-oriented at first; internal versus external consumption still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah: What is the sanctity of guidance given the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore targets versus about INR3,600 crore actual, and the OCF miss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said the INR4,500 crore target implied about 55% growth, and blamed a large EV two-wheeler customer dropping about 90% of volume plus government project delays. On OCF, it said standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore while the metering business drove the consolidated outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Nitin Arora: Why no guidance, and what will move the INR600 crore negative OCF to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it now commits to outgrowing the market at twice market growth rather than a number. It expects the INR600 crore negative to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations the key lever.

qa_highlights.question: Renu Baid Pugalia: Share of metering in revenue, growth ex-metering, rail ramp-up and government-offtake risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering is about 20-25% of revenue, but about 60% of that business was already EMS supply. EV grew about 28%. Kavach has initial approval and trial orders, with H1 approvals and H2 bulk orders expected; rail growth of 20-25% is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Amber Singhania: Metering subsidiary revenue, EBITDA and receivables; why receivables rose despite the securitisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering revenue was INR971 crore and receivables about INR1,365 crore. Securitisation has only started with one bank, with about INR40 crore discounted in each of two quarters, because the bank needs first-month billing and collections; installation delays are the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Dhaval Somaiya: Pending meter count, and breakup of the other roughly INR740 crore of subsidiary revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending supply to be completed in 2-3 months, with a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension. Of the EMS revenue of INR2,655 crore, two foreign entities contributed about INR300 crore on average, and KEMPL is the main EMS subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Sumant Kumar: Why did intangibles rise by about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics capitalised about INR320 crore of intangibles. Amortisation was booked once in Q4 (about INR32 crore), and will now be booked quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: Do the INR1,000 crore OSAT and INR500 crore PCB production targets still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Kunhikannan said no such guidance was given. He estimated FY27 PCB output at INR300-400 crore and OSAT at INR250-300 crore, both export-led.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash flow: metering receivables of about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current; securitisation has discounted only about INR80 crore cumulatively.
Guidance credibility: the company missed its INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue targets, and the CFO was unavailable for the call due to health reasons.
Top management restructuring and role realignment flagged during the quarter.
Customer concentration: a large EV two-wheeler customer fell about 90%.
Government payment and installation dependency for smart metering; DISCOM and GENCO timelines.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles now recurs (about INR32 crore per quarter), which will depress PAT.
Auto industry outlook downgraded; OSAT and PCB ramp and internal versus external sales mix still undecided.
543664|2026-03.management_tone: Defensive and apologetic on the guidance miss and cash flow, while confident on the EMS business, OSAT and PCB growth. Management was evasive on specific FY27 revenue and cash targets, offering market-relative growth and quarterly updates instead.
key_quotes: We did an aggressive top line growth in the year based on the order book and we got the electrification of the vehicle.
As I said, it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order. We sincerely apologize for that this has happened.
We are committing for our growth based on what market can pull in.
Our order book continues to be stronger at INR9,000 crores plus.
I think the inflection point has stopped and will come into the reduction, and we will come back in 3 quarters with positive results on specifically this entity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 operational EBITDA margin was 15.6% and FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.8%, but quarterly intangible amortisation of about INR32 crore now recurs and metering mix is lower-margin, so margin gains are conditional on OSAT/PCB ramp and NPD mix reaching the targeted ~30% of revenue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for OSAT Unit 2; PCB first year in FY27
rows.why: OSAT Unit 2 is set to commercialise by Q2 FY27 and FY27 production estimates are INR250-300 crore OSAT and INR300-400 crore PCB, with a INR9,000 crore+ order book and OSAT revenue visibility above INR2,500 crore over five years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management commits to growing at about 2x the EMS market (15-18% market growth implies roughly 30-36%), EV grew 28% in FY26 despite a ~90% drop at one customer, and FY26 EMS revenue grew about 26-30% to INR2,655 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed directly; FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore mainly through acquisitions, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is conditional on OSAT/PCB ramp and cash flow recovering.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Company missed INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue guidance with FY26 at INR3,626 crore, has no numeric FY27 target, and the CFO was absent from the call, so an upgrade is unlikely to be offered soon.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow was about INR600 crore negative against marginally negative guidance, metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore with only about INR80 crore securitised, and auto outlook was cut to single-digit or low double-digit growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three products are already in production (SOP started), the product launch cycle has shortened to 9 months from 12-18, and NPD-led revenue targets nearly 30% of total revenue; Kavach rail approvals expected in H1 FY27 with bulk orders in H2.

rows.label: Metering receivables collection and securitisation
rows.why: Management expects the INR600 crore negative OCF to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations and collections as the key lever; metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore.

rows.label: Standalone EMS working capital days improvement
rows.why: Standalone EMS working capital days fell to 53 from 83 in FY24 and standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore versus INR65 crore last year.

rows.label: Kavach rail bulk orders
rows.when: H1 FY27 approvals, H2 FY27 bulk orders
rows.why: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

tone.note: Management was apologetic and evasive on the missed INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance and the negative OCF, while confident on EMS, OSAT, PCB and rail; analysts pressed on guidance sanctity, metering receivables, securitisation and intangible amortisation.

543664|2026-06.headline: Kaynes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% to INR946 crore and EBITDA rose 31% to INR147.6 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore as inventory and metering receivables rose.
543664|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR946 crore, driven by EMS (standalone EMS up 53%, overseas up 327% on the August Electronics acquisition), while smart metering fell 12% YoY to about INR204 crore as management deliberately curbed supplies over collections. EBITDA was INR147.6 crore at a 15.6% margin, with management flagging margin pressure from component and PCB cost inflation and lead times of 6 to 8 months. Negative operating cash flow was about INR259 crore (management also cited INR235 crore in another bridge), with inventory up about INR177 crore and receivables up about INR68 crore. OSAT and PCB commissioning remains guided for Q3 FY27, with a FY27 revenue target of INR450 to 500 crore across both.

segments.name: EMS (overall, incl. overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR854 crore including GST, with 40% overall EMS growth and about 48% growth cited by management; collections of INR847 crore. Receivables in EMS were about INR613 crore at quarter end versus INR606 crore at the start.

segments.name: Smart metering (GridCrest)
segments.commentary: Sales about INR240 crore including GST against collections of INR88 crore, so production and supply were halted. Metering receivables rose from INR1,158 crore to INR1,311 crore; about INR200 crore was received in early July.

segments.name: OSAT (Kaynes Semicon)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR700 crore; government subsidy of INR170 crore received till July 2026. Commercial billing expected from Q3 FY27; Unit 2 on track for operation by Q3 FY27. Mitsui partnership for Japan access announced.

segments.name: PCB (Kaynes Circuit)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR500 crore, with about INR250 crore in transit. Commercial production to start next quarter; one global customer has requested the entire capacity and trials are ongoing with a vendor code approved.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth committed at 2x the market growth; no absolute top-line number given. Market grew about 17% in Q1.
OSAT and PCB combined FY27 revenue target INR450 to 500 crore, with revenue starting from Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex plan: about INR300 crore OSAT, about INR300 crore PCB and about INR250 crore EMS; Q1 spend about INR230 crore in total across these.
Management expects profitability to take a couple of quarters to normalise; FY27 described as a difficult, tough year.
Management expects receivables turnaround in the metering business and cash-positive position by end of FY27.
Working capital to be reported on a rolling 12-month basis going forward.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR180 crore (per management in the call), against a broader plan of about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and about INR250 crore for EMS.
Capex in FY26 was INR473 crore for OSAT and INR324 crore for PCB.
Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on track to be operational by Q3 FY27, despite minor slippage from West Asia-related equipment and logistics disruption.
Government subsidy of INR170 crore received in OSAT till July 2026, with more subsidies expected to fund further capex.

First 3U satellite in prototype; launch targeted mid-next year pending regulatory testing and an ISRO launch date (PSLV or GSLV). Titanium gas bottle manufacturing via Crio Precision and Aerotech for ISRO and DRDO.
demand_pricing: Order book of more than INR8,900 crore; management said Q1 order additions exceeded deliveries.

New logos include a second-largest Indian two-wheeler EV maker (serial supply begun after about 8 months of development), German and French global brands, and a leading Indian wireless operator; management cited about 72 customer visits in the quarter.
Component prices up about 30% to 35% per management; PCB prices up about 3x; lead times more than 6 to 8 months in some categories; PCB suppliers demanding advance payment.
FX impact on imports about 3.3% of import level, per management.
Pass-through to customers is on a quarter-on-quarter basis and may lag; management said agreements with strategic customers allow some price pass-through.
Aerospace recovered in the quarter; management said growth was seen across railways, automotive, aerospace and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMS growth excluding metering, and what is the EBITDA bridge and metering strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EMS grew 40% and metering 28% (per one answer), with standalone EMS up 53% and metering down 12%. Lower other income after QIP proceeds (about 2.5 points on PBT/PAT) and higher depreciation were cited for margin pressure. Management said it is exploring models to divest the service portion of metering to keep receivables off the balance sheet, with details promised by February.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash flow from operations and metering revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was negative about INR259 crore (inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore), versus negative INR379 crore in Q1 FY26. Another bridge given later cited INR235 crore; the company's cash profit was about INR158 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables, inventory and payables figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables (current and non-current) rose from about INR1,765 crore to INR1,925 crore. Inventory days were about 105 at Q1 end versus 96 earlier. Management said the 12-month rolling receivable days were about 163 and the quarterly figure about 190.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth and the OSAT/PCB FY27 and FY28 scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to 2x market growth without an absolute number, citing market volatility. OSAT and PCB together are targeted at INR450 to 500 crore of FY27 revenue from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of component cost inflation is captured and will gross margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX impact was about 3.3% of imports and back-to-back customer pass-through covers most of the rest, but pass-through may lag by a quarter. Ramesh Kunhikannan said FY27 would be a tough year with margins under pressure, though planned requirements would be met.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and PCB margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex plan is about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and INR250 crore for EMS, with about INR230 crore spent in Q1. Management declined to give PCB margin or ROCE targets, saying it was too early and disputing that PCB margins had fallen.

financial_highlights.change: vs negative INR379 crore in Q1 FY26
management cited ~INR9,000 crore earlier in call

financial_highlights.value: about INR800 crore (approximate, to be confirmed)

risks_watch: Cash conversion: operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore (another bridge cited INR235 crore), with inventory up INR177 crore; watch whether metering receivables of INR1,311 crore convert and whether the cash-positive target by end FY27 is met.

Margin pressure: component prices up 30-35%, PCB prices up about 3x, lead times 6-8 months, and pass-through to customers lags by a quarter; management said FY27 is a tough year and profitability may take a couple of quarters to normalise.
OSAT and PCB commissioning: Unit 2 and Circuit Chennai guided for Q3 FY27 after West Asia-related slippage; FY27 revenue target INR450-500 crore for both depends on this timeline.
Metering strategy: management is exploring models to divest the service portion to keep receivables off balance sheet, with details promised by February; no concrete plan yet.
Debt and tax clarity: total debt was given as approximately INR800 crore, to be confirmed; consolidated effective tax rate about 35% versus about 23% standalone.
key_quotes: We expect this could take a couple of quarters for profitability to normalize and return to the levels as we had earlier committed to.
Yes, its a difficult year. This year is a difficult year, but I don't think for us whatever we have planned, we will try and meet the requirement. But it is not going to be an easy year.
we are pretty confident that we will be able to do the turnaround by end of this year in terms of receivables from the metering business.
So we don't want to give an absolute number because there is so much of volatility in the market.
543664|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on EMS growth and cash turnaround commitments but cautious on FY27 margins, calling it a difficult, tough year. It was evasive on PCB margin and ROCE targets, on metering divestment structure and on exact debt figures, deferring these to later updates.

543667|2026-03.headline: Inox Green Q4 FY26 total income INR120 crore (+40% YoY), EBITDA INR57 crore (+93%), with INR40 crore of acquisition-linked other income flattering profit.
543667|2026-03.overview: Inox Green reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR120 crore, EBITDA of INR57 crore, PBT of INR46 crore and PAT of INR28 crore, with machine availability near 96.5%. Management said roughly INR40 crore of quarterly other income relates to the two pending O&M acquisitions (debt-linked income), with INR10 crore each from value-added services and treasury. Parent Inox Wind reported Q4 revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY) and PAT of INR106 crore, and FY26 revenue of about INR4,500–4,600 crore against a revised INR5,000 crore target. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% and Inox Green EBITDA of above INR600 crore, while the evacuation-infrastructure demerger has been approved by NCLT Ahmedabad.

financial_highlights.metric: Inox Green other income (Q4 FY26, consolidated)
Inox Wind EBITDA / PBT / PAT (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.value: INR333 crore / INR216 crore / INR106 crore
INR4,500 crore (about INR4,600 crore cited against INR5,000 crore target)

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 EBITDA INR57 crore on INR120 crore total income; portfolio above 13 GWp (about 10.5 GW wind, rest solar). Management said full-year turnover of INR426 crore gave EBITDA of about INR210 crore, roughly 50% margin, and Devansh Jain put the ex-acquisition-income margin at about 45%.

segments.name: Inox Wind (EPC/equipment)
segments.commentary: Q4 consolidated revenue INR1,306 crore (flat YoY) and EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26. Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to reach 75–80% equipment supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (management also cited around 70–75%); Devansh Jain implied about INR7,500 crore revenue on the INR4,500 crore base.
Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crore, maintained after the investments fold into Inox Green's balance sheet.
EBITDA margin for Inox Wind guided at north of about 20%.

Inox Green expected to see a multifold rise in consolidated EBITDA and PAT in FY27 over FY26 once the two O&M acquisitions (about 6.5 GW) are consolidated; the first entity's order is expected within about two weeks, the second within 60–90 days.

Demerger of evacuation infrastructure business (gross block about INR1,000 crore, annual depreciation INR50–55 crore) into Inox Renewable Solutions expected to complete in about 1–2 months; dividend policy to follow consolidation.
New 4.4 MW turbine launch expected within calendar 2026, subject to approvals.
Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding roughly 3 GW+ per year, of which 20–30% expected to be wind.
capex_capacity: Inox Green portfolio above 13 GWp, of which about 10.5 GW is wind; acquisition of about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets from two companies is pending, with one entity's order expected in about two weeks.
Inox Wind's 3.1 GW order book supports more than 24 months of execution visibility; most EPC jobs expected to be complete by H1 FY27 except one leading job.
Backward integration: cranes about half in-house with a couple more coming this year; power transformer capacity ramped up; power electronics expansion planned.
Inox Clean: 10 GW IPP, 10 GW solar cell and 10 GW module targeted over next 15 months; about 2 GW installed IPP capacity; 6 GW module and 3 GW cell manufacturing capacity.
demand_pricing: Inox Wind order book 3.1 GW, of which about 500 MW is from Inox Clean (about 16%); Inox Clean orders expected to rise to about one-third of annual execution.
Management said equipment supply carries better working-capital terms (mostly LC-backed) and steel pass-through, and margins are more protected than in turnkey EPC.
Inox Green O&M margin about 50%; O&M expected to rise from about 10% to 18–20% of consolidated revenue after acquisitions.
PSU contracts saw payment delays; management said the PSU project issue is now resolved.
Working capital: management said net working capital days target of about 200 was missed; supply disruption for a key imported component (ECS) by ship and commodity price rises were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin do the acquired O&M assets carry, and what is the FY27 Inox Green guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions have about 50% EBITDA margin as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems; FY27 Inox Green EBITDA guidance is above INR600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR600 crore FY27 EBITDA reached given acquisition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said entity one's order is due in about two weeks and entity two's within 60–90 days; revenues and profits from 1 April 2026 will be reflected in consolidated results. Management added about 1.5 GW of organic addition for Inox Wind plus value-added services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 other income about INR61 crore, and how much is core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions' debt, INR10 crore to value-added services and INR10 crore to treasury; PAT impact about INR25–26 crore. Devansh Jain said ex-acquisition income the margin would be about 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall from INR78–82 crore in Q3 to INR69 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarter-on-quarter move to value-added service lumpiness of about INR8–9 crore and asked investors to look at the annualised run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Inox Wind moving from turnkey to equipment supply, and what happens to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Agarwal said turnkey caused the largest working capital blockage; order book moved from 100% turnkey to about 50:50, targeting 75–80% equipment supply. Management said margins stay above about 20% and equipment supply is more predictable.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 megawatt execution and status of working capital days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY26 megawatt execution, reiterating revenue-based guidance; it reported INR4,600 crore against a INR5,000 crore target and said INR400 crore would be made up in Q1–Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and use of INR600 crore cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said the Board will set a dividend policy after consolidation; the INR600 crore is expected to be operating cash flow with no depreciation or finance cost and a tax shield up to INR700 crore; acquisitions may use 10–20% of free cash flow.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: Inox Wind working capital and receivables (PSU delays) are behind the INR400 crore shortfall versus target; watch Q1 FY27 collections.
Quality of Inox Green earnings: about INR40 crore of Q4 other income is acquisition-linked; ex-that, margin is about 45% on annual basis.

543687|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 20% to Rs 1,138 crore and EBITDA 34% to Rs 101 crore, while branded formulation grew only 3%.

543720|2026-03.headline: KFin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23% YoY (4.6% ex-Ascent) as mark-to-market hits and weak Issuer Solutions held EBITDA margin to 37%; FY27 guide 23-24% revenue growth.
543720|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew about 23% YoY but fell 6.3% QoQ, and ex-Ascent growth was only 4.6% YoY. Mark-to-market losses on equity and metal-ETF-driven asset mix shifts, plus weaker Issuer Solutions retail folios and corporate actions, weighed on the quarter. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 37% in Q4 (ex-Ascent about 42%), and core PAT rose 3.8% YoY in the quarter and 6.2% for FY26 to INR353 crore. Management guided to conservative FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23-24%, EBITDA growth of 16-17% (margin near 39-40%) and PAT growth of about 10%, and said it will recalibrate monthly.

AUM grew in line with industry at about 21%, but revenue grew about 11% due to April 2025 pricing discounts, MTM erosion and ETF mix shift.

segments.name: Issuer Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributes 10% of Q4 revenue; both revenue and segment profit fell YoY. Management cited retail folio exodus (existing clients lost about 1.7 million folios vs 2.5-3 million added through new wins), tepid corporate actions and a base effect from a large Q4 FY25 demerger.

segments.name: AIF, private wealth and PMS
segments.commentary: Contributes 4.5% of Q4 revenue. AIF AUM grew about 19-24% and AIF fund count rose from 593 to 741, with margins above 37%; private wealth/PMS revenue fell on MTM, though 6 wealth platform wins were signed early in the year.

segments.commentary: Contributes about 15% of Q4 revenue at 8% EBITDA margin; about 499 new fund-manager clients added (about 900-950 funds). Management expects Ascent revenue growth of 25-30% and margin to move to the early teens over time.

segments.commentary: Each about 1.5% of Q4 revenue. NPS AUM-linked pricing moved from per-subscriber to basis points, and pension subscribers grew about 34% vs industry 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic MF yield decline of about 4-5% YoY in FY27 still hold if metal mix stabilises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance assumes the same asset mix as end-FY26 with ETFs around 23%; it expects more active funds this year, and the 4-5% yield view was not directly reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state Issuer Solutions revenue growth after one-offs, given realisations hit harder than folios?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to net folio loss (about 1.7 million existing folios lost), weak corporate actions in Q4, and a demerger base effect; it expects these to normalise from Q1 FY27 with demergers pushed from March into May.

qa_highlights.question: Why does FY27 EBITDA guidance imply margin below 40% after Ascent consolidation?

543720|2026-06.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
543720|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik (Indus Capital): What cost takeouts drove better domestic MF segment margins despite single-digit revenue growth and yield compression, and can segment margins bottom out if yields stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited technology-led cost optimisation across payroll, non-payroll and licensing, not ad-hoc cuts; full increments were given this year. It said yield is driven by pricing/discounts, asset mix and AMC growth, and that pricing-driven stability is expected from here, with the SIP automation and next FinEx launch (by end calendar 2026) as controllable margin levers.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik: how much of the PAT gap (about INR 47 million between INR 799 million and INR 752 million) narrows via cost takeouts versus revenue growth, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is both, weighted more to top-line growth at Ascent (EBITDA about 7-8%), while KFin-level cost optimisation will do the heavy lifting. PAT pressure is largely non-cash amortisation of goodwill/contract payments and capitalised One Constellation platform costs.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab Mukherjee (360 ONE): Is the yield drop only debt-to-liquid mix, how should yield be modelled over the remaining three quarters given ~2% QoQ fall, and how will bolt-on wins add revenue?

Bolt-on deals of about INR 40 crore signed in Q1 run for 3, 6 and 15 months and are episodic, not annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab: why did international ex-Ascent revenue fall QoQ, and how should it be modelled?

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Bagga (DSP MF): what is the split of the yield decline between debt-to-liquid mix and renegotiation provisions, and will Ascent margins reach double digits next quarter?

Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue, and retail participation remains weak. Management opened FY27 with an order book of about INR310 crore, all slated for execution within roughly three quarters, and signalled a push into combat drones (loitering munitions, strike UAVs) alongside its ISR core. 543932|2026-06.headline: ideaForge Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR68.6 crore from INR12.8 crore, with EBITDA positive at INR4.3 crore and gross margin at 49%.

Management also highlighted a INR500 crore QIP, a Letter of Intent for up to INR151 crore for YETI, and a larger defence procurement pipeline, but gave no order-inflow or US revenue numbers.

543957|2026-03.headline: RedTape FY26 revenue rose 19.6% to INR2,415 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 19% from 17.5%, with standalone PAT of INR244 crores.
543957|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year where the business absorbed a weak first half and then accelerated in Q3 and Q4, helped by the GST cut on footwear below INR2,500. Q4 revenue was INR674 crores with a 43.4% gross margin and standalone PAT of INR71 crores. Management attributed the lower reported gross margin to e-commerce rebates now netted against top-line, with other income carrying these rebates. Working capital improved: debt fell about INR200 crores from September to March and operating cash flow was stated at INR175 crores, though inventory days remain high at about 170.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR1,535 crores in FY26, about 63% of revenue; remains the footfall anchor, with casual and athleisure growing within it.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: INR805 crores in FY26, about 34% of revenue; management is investing most here for FY27, including women's apparel. Segment margin not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: INR75 crores in FY26, about 3% of revenue; sunglasses, hard luggage and grooming grew faster than the other segments from a small base.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: Ozark (outdoor/adventure) response exceeded expectations and store rollout is being scaled. Bond Street and Mode were launched in FY26; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 200-250 stores in FY27 (500-1,500 sq ft), with COCO share of 25-35% and the rest FOFO; expansion into South and West India.
Inventory target of 150 days, described as 'very near future'; management earlier said it could settle at 120-150 days.
EBITDA margin band guided at 16-19%, described as a 'new normal' rather than a peak.
No MRP increase planned for the next 3-6 months; raw-material cost volatility to be reassessed after September.
Long-term target of 65-70% of revenue from retail (offline); no multi-year revenue target given.
capex_capacity: Store count crossed 550 (223 exclusive showrooms across 161 cities at year-end per prepared remarks); about 70% of stores in North India, present in 300 cities.
Seven marketplace warehouses in India, with plans to open two more; Ludhiana warehouse opened in FY26.
Unnao warehouse expanded by about 3 lakh sq ft; remaining capex went to retail expansion. Management referenced about INR450 crores of prior capex without a FY26 breakdown.
Store economics: in the franchise (FOFO) model, the franchisee bears rent, salaries, miscellaneous costs and fixtures capex; RedTape keeps billing and top line.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: offline retail about 70% of turnover; online (e-commerce and quick commerce) about 30%, primarily via Flipkart and Myntra on a marketplace model.
Management cites RedTape as the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra; online repeat customers at 54-58%.
Pricing: no MRP hikes yet; company works on cost-plus and has about six months of POs and LCs covered.
Management said the Q4 volume lift was not only GST-driven, citing wedding season, healthy footfalls and same-store growth; SSSG was 17.8% in Q4.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns hold the majority of stores; consumer shift to organised branded product cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high (about 175 days on sales, over 300 days on COGS) and where will it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory peaked above 250 days and is now about 170, driven by marketplace warehouse build-out and offline expansion. The target is 120-150 days, with 150 as the ideal near-term level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA improved, and what is the medium-term EBITDA view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce rebates are now netted against revenue, so the gross margin decline is top-line driven, with no PBT impact. CFO said EBITDA has hovered around 16-18%, with 19% described as a new normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of INR133 crores and the FY25 restatement?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR88 crores is e-commerce discounts/rebates and the rest is claims from platforms. The FY25 restatement was an accounting change, applied to the prior year as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the apparel margin and the operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not report footwear and apparel margins separately and did not give a figure. On cash flow, CFO said operating cash flow reached INR175 crores and debt fell about INR200 crores since September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin, the COCO/FOFO split, and the accessories strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is about 16.4%. About 25-27% of stores are COCO. Accessories expansion is framed as raising wallet share and SSSG, building on belts, wallets and caps.

qa_highlights.question: Payable days appear to have dropped sharply; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially deferred the question and the CFO said he would revert, citing payable days history of about 171-188 days in recent years.

risks_watch: Inventory at about 170 days versus the 150-day target; operating cash flow and short-term borrowings depend on this.
Payable days reportedly fell sharply (about 55 days per an analyst's reading); management has not yet explained this.
Raw material cost pressure; price increases are deferred until after September, and no price hikes are taken.
Gross margin optics shaped by e-commerce rebate accounting; EBITDA margin band is wide (16-19%).
Apparel margin not disclosed, and the segment is now 34% of revenue and the focus of FY27 investment.
Store expansion of 200-250 outlets in FY27 must clear return thresholds from day one, per management.

rows.why: No MRP increase planned for 3-6 months with raw-material cost volatility to be reassessed after September, so pricing is not a near-term lever.

543957|2026-06.headline: Redtape Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 19.4% YoY to INR47 crore on 3.7% revenue growth to INR480 crore, with no price hikes and e-commerce deliberately de-prioritised.
543957|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 3.7% YoY to INR480 crore, with gross margin at 47.5% and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited >200 bps improvement; management attributed it to retail margins, operating leverage and supply chain
down from around INR28 crore in Q1 FY26, due to lower e-commerce platform rebates

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: 56% of Q1 turnover; management says footwear carries Q1 and Q2 while apparel peaks in Q3 and Q4. Open footwear ASPs improved sequentially.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 turnover; seasonally stronger in Q3 and Q4. Category-wise YoY growth not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 turnover. Sunglasses are in about 80% of stores; hard luggage in only 10-15% of stores as the category has shifted online.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Declined YoY because management declined incremental marketplace discounting. Online share fell to 22% from 30%. Management aspires to return to 30%.

segments.name: Core India retail
segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

segments.name: Sprandi (new brand)
segments.commentary: Sports brand acquired in April 2026 for India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and other countries. Shoes first, then apparel. Launch in India online and retail by end-September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.
EBITDA margin to be kept stable at around 20% for the year; management also expressed aspiration to increase margins.
Revenue growth: management hopes to continue the growth rate of the last 3-4 years; no quantified FY27 guidance.
E-commerce share expected to recover towards 30% of revenue; management called the Q1 dip a one-off.
Inventory target to reduce from 173 days to 150 days. Inventory build-up expected in Q2 ahead of festive season.
No MRP increases planned; management aims to offset cost inflation through efficiencies.

New store formats are mostly 800-1,500 sq ft, as expansion into South, East and West India is more store-count intensive.
Store in Forum Mall, Kolkata opened; malls to be used where they are stronger than high streets, particularly in South and West India.
Inventory at 173 days; Q2 build-up expected, then reduction in Q3 and Q4.
No acquisitions in the pipeline at present; management is open to opportunities in footwear and apparel.
demand_pricing: Demand was soft early in Q1 due to macro headwinds and cautious consumer spending, then improved through the quarter.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

risks_watch: E-commerce recovery to 30% of revenue is an aspiration; online share is 22% and management gave no timeline or quantified discount threshold, and the Q1 dip could persist into the BBD/festive season if marketplace discounting stays deep.

Margin stability: management aims to hold EBITDA margin around 20% and gross margin gains (>200 bps per analyst) were attributed mainly to retail margins without a category-level split, so sustainability is unverified.

Inflation exposure: minimum wage hikes in manufacturing states and war-linked input costs were absorbed without MRP increases; no quantification given, so a squeeze on margins if efficiencies fade is a watch item.
Store rollout: 33 stores opened in Q1 versus a FY27 aspiration of about 150-plus (earlier 200-250); new 800-1,500 sq ft formats in South, East and West India may ramp more slowly.
Inventory at 173 days with a Q2 build-up planned ahead of festive season; reduction to 150 days targeted, and non-BIS inventory remains outstanding.

Income tax search (September 2025) ongoing; management said it could take 2-3 years, with no material claim identified so far. Other income fell to INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore on lower e-commerce rebates.

We would like to believe it's a one-off thing.
Not really. It's a regular business for us.
We would like to remain as it is now. We'd like to be stable.
But as of now there's been no claim of any material and there's no risk of any material.

543959|2026-03.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
543959|2026-03.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

financial_highlights.metric: Return on average AUM / average tangible equity

segments.name: MSME loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR 8,873 crore, 79% of book, with Q4 disbursements of INR 785 crore. Average ticket size remains below INR 2.5 lakh and LTV is about 56-57%.

segments.name: Loan against gold
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,374 crore, 21% of book, growing 63% YoY; management says growth is mainly price-driven and the share may move toward 25%. Around 220 of 251 branches are pure gold branches.

segments.name: Co-origination (with ICICI)
segments.commentary: Co-origination was 16% of Q4 disbursements and 18-19% of AUM, and is expected to hold similar levels through FY27.

Spreads expected to hold at around 9% current level; over 90% of the book is variable-rate.
Opex expected to fall 20-25 bps through FY27 as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected to stay range-bound around 1.38%, with possible benefit of about 5 bps.
Branch network to stabilise at about 275 (from 251) during the year; 46 branches were added in FY26 against 25 guided.
Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected at 75:25; co-origination at 18-19% of AUM.
Capital: at 33% CRAR, growth could run about 2 years before needing fresh capital, with CRAR falling to about 24-26%.

Branch expansion is gated by state profitability; new states are run slowly for 18-24 months before scaling, with about 60% of branches older than 3 years.
Currently present in about one-fourth of districts in operating states (about 30% per Aseem Dhru) across 15 states.
Management says it will not add DSAs or connectors for at least two years; direct model retained.
Leverage at 1.9x debt/equity; management says capital is sufficient for roughly two years of growth.
demand_pricing: Management said growth in gold has been mostly price-driven rather than tonnage-driven; gold prices are expected to stay range-bound or flat.
Disbursements have been soft YoY; management said it paused momentum in some South, East and West pockets, and could return to around INR 300 crore per month when conditions improve.
South disbursals and AUM grew more slowly last year, which lifted the West's share of AUM (management said mix to stay similar for two quarters).
Early April data showed no new stress in sectors hit by LPG and fertilizer pressures; bounce rates marginally lower.
Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27; G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged.

qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

risks_watch: Macro shocks: oil price pass-through, weaker rupee, poor monsoon/El Nino, Gulf remittance risk, all flagged by management.
Gold price reversal would slow the gold book, which is 21% of AUM and the main driver of growth.
Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).
Disbursement volumes are down YoY and branches added in gold and MSME may not reach productivity targets as planned.
Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
543959|2026-09.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.

Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.

543960|2026-06.headline: Concord Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR257 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32% and PAT at INR58 crores.
543960|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached INR257 crores (+26% YoY), led by API at INR219 crores (+42%) while formulations fell 23% to INR39 crores, which management attributed to lost Middle East supplies. Exports grew 46% and domestic grew 12%. EBITDA rose 34% to INR82 crores (32% margin, +190 bps), and gross margin was 78.9%. Management said part of the growth was spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays, and that the injectable facility and Stellon Biotech are still at a nascent stage.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crores, up 42% YoY. Growth reported across immunosuppressants, anti-infectives, oncology and antifungals; anti-infectives and oncology grew faster than immunosuppressants.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, down 23% YoY. Management attributed the decline to Middle East customers buying API instead of formulation in Q1; ex-Middle East, domestic double-digit growth in both Intra (nephrology) and INCA (critical care) divisions.

segments.name: CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: Currently about 1-2% of revenue. One product commercialised in animal health (US, ANDA), currently a couple of million dollars in sales; management aims for double-digit share over time.

segments.name: Injectables
segments.commentary: Facility commercialised; utilisation about 5% in the quarter. Own branded generics supplied in-house; contract manufacturing discussions advanced, with some commercial onboarding expected in 2H FY27. Emerging-market sales expected from next year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth in FY27 to exceed the company's historical growth rates, citing visibility for coming quarters.
Spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays expected to continue into subsequent quarters; not quantified.
Long-term view: INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure in about 5-6 years, split roughly INR600-700 crores formulations and INR2,200 crores API.
EBITDA margin expected to exceed sales growth in FY27; 40% margin target expected to be reached partly in FY27 and more fully in FY28, dependent on injectable and Stellon ramp-up.
Two to three new product launches planned annually; a couple of advanced-stage products expected to commercialise in coming quarters.
Injectable facility expected to reach emerging-market sales next year after 12-15 month approval processes.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Unit 1 about 80% (analyst later cited 78%); Unit 2 about 25% (analyst later cited 55%); Unit 3 about 55% (includes some KSM manufacturing).
Unit 3 has about 160 acres, with only 20-25% of land used; capacity expansion decision expected at around 80-85% utilisation.
Approximately 1,250 m3 (cited as 1,250-metre cube) fermentation capacity; oncology products run in 5,000-litre fermenters at Unit 1.
Injectable facility: WHO GMP set, validation batches completed, customer audits underway; facility can do close to INR600 crores top line; utilisation about 5%.
Softgel facility added in oral solids; Unit 2 formulation facility at Valthera received NDA Uganda and PPB Kenya inspections; Limbasi facility passed ANVISA inspection.
Possible dedicated fermentation capacity for peptides and veterinary products if growth is needed ahead of the 80-85% threshold.
demand_pricing: Wallet share gains in the quarter were primarily price-driven on existing products, based on economies of scale from fermentation capacity; seeds were sown 8-12 months earlier.
Exports up 46% across Europe, Japan, LatAm and the US; US ANDA approvals received for mycophenolate mofetil and tofacitinib tablets.
Nystatin and fusidic acid (launched FY26, Europe-focused, awaiting CEP) cited as growing products with limited competition.
Management reported no customer concerns on the reported proposed US tariff on generics.
Constant-currency context: USD movement about 10-12% YoY; net impact after input costs about 3-5% flowing to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is normalisation of delayed procurement versus structural gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Some spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays contributed; most growth came from new products across all geographies. Similar spillovers are expected in subsequent quarters, though not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: INR600-700 crores from formulations and INR2,200 crores from APIs, expected in about 5-6 years at the current CAGR. Unit 3 has room to expand once utilisation reaches 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and CDMO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 80%, Unit 3 about 55%, Unit 2 about 25%. CDMO is about 1-2% of revenue, with a target of double digits over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic formulations decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior-year quarter included Middle East supplies that did not recur. Ex-Middle East, domestic formulations grew double digits in both divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the wallet share gain attributed to pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing advantage from fermentation scale was passed to customers, and margins were held. Softer factors, such as fermentation partnership, were secondary.

qa_highlights.question: When will the injectable facility reach EBITDA breakeven and emerging-market sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable utilisation is about 5%; breakeven utilisation was not given and will be followed up. Emerging-market sales expected next year after a 12-15 month approval process; contract manufacturing sales expected in 2H FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 40% EBITDA margin by end of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage and renewable energy should drive margins above sales growth. Full 40% depends on injectable and Stellon ramp-up, so it may slip into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How can API revenue reach INR2,200 crores without new capacity, given Unit 1 and Unit 2 utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 is the focus for 8-10 pipeline anti-infective and antifungal products. Oncology revenue is high value per litre, so utilisation understates revenue potential. Capacity utilisation for Unit 3 excluding KSMs is slightly above the 20-25% estimate the analyst gave.

So we stand on track to achieving growth better than our historical growth rates.

543963|2026-03.headline: Shelter Pharma FY26 revenue rose 44% to INR 73.13 Cr with PAT of INR 9.03 Cr; management targets INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030.
543963|2026-03.overview: Shelter Pharma reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 73.13 Cr (up 44% YoY), EBITDA of INR 12.72 Cr (margin 17.39%, up 26% YoY) and PAT of INR 9.03 Cr (up 25% YoY). Q4 revenue was INR 39.84 Cr (up 50% YoY) and exports were about INR 6 Cr (up 164%). Management is expanding sales teams and distributors, which has compressed margins from roughly 20-21% in FY24-FY25, and working capital has stretched to 234 days with operating cash flow of minus INR 12.48 Cr. Management reiterated the INR 200 Cr FY2030 revenue target and outlined a second plant near Ahmedabad, with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr.

segments.name: Veterinary (animal health)
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 revenue. Leading products include Feedvet multivitamin powder, Lactocal calcium gel, Vymet D3+E liquid, Diarub bolus and Livodin liquid.

segments.name: Human healthcare
segments.commentary: About 45% of FY26 revenue. Key brands are Lemon & Barley Water (about INR 3.0-3.5 Cr revenue, no direct competition claimed), Sherolax, Gashoshel, Meryn, Joemega, All Vitamins and Omega-3 capsules. Management says human and veterinary margins are similar.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR 6 Cr in FY26, up 164%, mainly Africa and Middle East (UAE, Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Yemen, Sudan). Management says export margins are 20-25% higher than domestic; over INR 5 Cr already reached in Q1 FY27 per management.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target of about INR 200 Cr by FY2030, which management called 'actual numbers, not that conservative'.
Revenue mix goal of 40-45% human healthcare with similar margins.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around current levels (~17%) this year or next, then rise to 22-25% over the next two to three years; management said it will not go below 17%.
Working capital days to fall from 234 to about 60 and then to about one month; management says FY27 growth of about 40% CAGR is 'absolutely possible'.
Second plant installation to begin around end-2027 (approvals from December 2026), with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr mostly funded from internal accruals.
No plan to raise capital currently; company is debt-free and will rely on internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Existing Himatnagar plant closed FY26 at about INR 75 Cr revenue; management says it can reach INR 100 Cr on the same plant.
Land near Ahmedabad acquired for a second manufacturing facility for about INR 2.5 Cr, funded from internal accruals.
Second plant: installation to start around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026; estimated capex INR 12-15 Cr.
Team: about 80 in sales, 12 in Ahmedabad office and 50 in the factory; sales team expected to double in two years.
Distribution: 12,000+ doctors reached and 5,000+ retail pharmacies; coverage expanded from 10-12 states to 15+ states, pan-India by FY27 per management.
demand_pricing: Management says the Ayurvedic market (INR 1,070 bn in 2025 to INR 3,728 bn by 2034, 15.52% CAGR) supports growth; organised players dominate value.
Verka Dairy order: minimum order value about INR 1-1.5 Cr initially, per management.
Africa, Middle East and state-government and central procurement (KPKB, CGHS, CSD) applications are being pursued; management says each African container is worth about INR 1-1.5 Cr.
Government and bulk supply margins were not quantified; management says bulk purchasing is used to build stock.
Export order book size was not disclosed; management will follow up via Financial Minds.

qa_highlights.question: Why are loans and advances on the balance sheet, and what is the return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said advances (about INR 37 Cr per an analyst's reading) are raw-material advances for long-term procurement and export pipeline orders; no return was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did promoter stake fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was internal structuring: a family member was exiting part of the stake, and the promoter is buying stakes; not a promoter stake sale.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East war hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pharma is treated as essential; three shipments are in transit to Africa and one to Dubai, with no margin impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 200 Cr target conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is realistic: exports were about INR 2.5 Cr in FY25 and about INR 6.5 Cr in FY26, with over INR 5 Cr already in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next plant and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR 12-15 Cr, mostly from internal accruals, with installation starting around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin down from about 20% to 17%, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to aggressive expansion in sales teams, channels and distributors; margins expected to stay similar this year or next, then rise to 22-25% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and working capital at 234 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved from advance payments in three states to credit terms in new states; credit days were cut from 120 to 90 and are targeted at 60, then about one month.

qa_highlights.question: Why was preference equity of INR 42.44 Cr issued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was mainly for working capital to fund a sales team that is expected to double in the next two years.

543965|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 3,032 crore (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA rose 37.5% to Rs 222 crore, with a record Rs 524 crore of new business wins.
543965|2026-03.overview: TVS SCS posted its first Rs 3,000-plus crore revenue quarter, with ISCS growing 17.5% YoY and GFS 34.8% YoY on India ocean freight volumes. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened 80 bps YoY to 7.3%, driven by the Europe turnaround in ISCS and India volume growth in GFS. Full-year revenue grew 10.1% to Rs 11,003 crore and adjusted PBT rose 166% to Rs 99.3 crore. Management guided ISCS margin to 9.5-10% and group margin to about 7.3-7.4% for FY27, with GFS rates the key swing factor. The CEO-designate's first call also marked the retirement of MD Ravi Viswanathan.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 2,283 crore (+17.5% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 8,238.9 crore (+9.6%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% in Q4, driven by Europe recovery and steady India growth; North America scaled up a large project live in H2 FY25.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected in double digits, possibly early-to-mid teens, with ISCS a strong contributor.
ISCS adjusted EBITDA margin expected at 9.5-10% in FY27, versus 9.3% in Q4 FY26.
Group adjusted EBITDA margin expected around 7.3-7.4% in FY27, dependent on GFS freight rate trajectory.
Medium term: ISCS margin of 10.5-11%; GFS margin to move toward about 5% within 4-8 quarters and settle at 6-6.5%.
Management expects PBT to grow sequentially every quarter; Swamy & Sons acquisition (completed in May 2026) expected to be margin accretive for India in FY27.
Depreciation and lease interest expected to change with a shift from long-term to short-term leases; ECL impairment expected slightly lower in FY27 than Rs 56 crore booked in FY26.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; capital allocation prioritised to ISCS, with minimal fixed-asset investment beyond warehouses.
Lease portfolio shifting from long-term to medium and short-term rentals where operationally feasible; short-term rental charges and warehouse R&M rose in FY26.
Second site of a key North America project went live in Q4 FY26, raising Ind AS 116 depreciation to Rs 108 crore in Q4.
Swamy & Sons 3PL acquisition (FMCG and consumption supply chains in India) completed in May 2026.
Patent accepted for unified logistics platform; AI and robotics deployed in operations.
Credit rating India AA.
demand_pricing: Q4 new business wins were Rs 523.7 crore, an all-time quarterly high (21% of Q4 FY25 revenue); FY26 new business Rs 1,206.7 crore (12.1% of FY25 revenue).
Order pipeline Rs 6,100 crore; typical conversion around 22%, with a target of 23-25%.
Fortune 500 active customers rose to 100 from 91, with 9 added in FY26.
Average customer contract length: about 4-4.1 years in India, 5+ years in North America, about 7.5 years in Europe.
GFS: freight rates under pressure; management says volumes are more resilient than pricing, which is volatile due to West Asia disruptions. Company says none of its lanes are in West Asia.
North America growing at about 28.3% CAGR over five years, focused on industrial and auto accounts, with a goal of $50-60 million per large customer over 3-4 years.
Sectors with momentum include power (alternate energy), aerospace and defence (MOU with ALA), and China-plus-one relocations, which are still early.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ISCS growth, potentially 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports it if conversion rises from about 22% to 23-25%. It set expectations at double-digit, early-to-mid-teens growth, and aspires to get closer to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: ISCS 9.5-10% from 9.3% in Q4; group about 7.3-7.4%, with GFS freight rates the main variable and management cautious on GFS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was part of the labour-code provision taken in Q4 rather than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: A Labour Ministry clarification on 16 March came after Q3 results, requiring a reassessment and a Rs 5.2 crore additional provision in Q4. The company says the clarifications are now fully provided for.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impairment loss on financial instruments of about Rs 17.6 crore, and what is the FY27 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an expected credit loss provision on customers, Rs 56 crore booked in FY26. Management expects the rate to be slightly lower in FY27, as most customers are highly rated B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China-plus-one opportunity material?
qa_highlights.answer: Early traction with existing customers, including an earthmoving equipment company, but deals are not yet deep. Management is waiting to see whether US buyers accelerate expansion in India.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term targets for GFS and group revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not endorse a Rs 15,000 crore target by FY29-30; its long-term aspiration is early-teens EBITDA margins, with the GFS margin reaching 6-6.5%, the leader deferring to the incoming CEO.

risks_watch: GFS freight rate volatility from West Asia disruptions; management says volumes are resilient but pricing is volatile.
Ability to lift the pipeline conversion rate from about 22% to 23-25%.
Sustaining the Europe recovery and the North America project ramp.
Labour code provisions still have grey areas and interpretation risk.
Leadership transition: MD Ravi Viswanathan retiring; Vikas Chadha (Global CEO and MD designate) takes over.
Lease cost trend and rising short-term rental and R&M costs in warehousing.
