543971|2026-03.headline: Bondada guides FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% on a INR7,147 crore order book; FY26 revenue reported at INR2,843 crore.
543971|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of about INR2,843 crore (vs INR1,571 crore in FY25) and a net profit of about INR211 crore, with the order book at INR7,147 crore as of 31 March 2026. Q4 EBITDA margin dipped on low-margin billing and higher steel and cable prices, which management says is not structural; FY26 margin rose about 30 bps to 7.5% from 7.2%. Cash from operations was positive at INR125 crore after collections above INR1,000 crore in Q4. New initiatives in BESS, data centres, defence and an IPP of 2 GW in Andhra Pradesh were highlighted as FY27 drivers.

segments.name: Renewable energy EPC
segments.commentary: Largest order book segment at INR4,536 crore (about 65% of total). About 1.3 GW commissioned cumulatively; about 0.5 GW commissioned in FY26 and target of about 1.5 GW in FY27, taking cumulative to about 3 GW.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR1,463 crore covering about 850 MW from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Tamil Nadu 400 MWh due in about one year (financially closed, Canara Bank funding); AP 450 MWh due in about 18 months, financial closure pending.

segments.name: Telecom (BSNL)
segments.commentary: About 1,536 BSNL towers installed and about 1,506 on-air (about 99% strike rate). Management is pursuing Kavach railway passive-infrastructure tenders, with first win from South Central Railway.

segments.name: Services / O&M
segments.commentary: Management said O&M rose from about INR90 crore to about INR140 crore in FY26. An analyst's reading of a segment drop from about INR356 crore to INR140 crore was disputed; management said it would recheck the segmental reporting.

segments.name: Products and defence
segments.commentary: Products are targeted to rise from about 10% to 30% of mix (EPC 90% to 70%). First defence order is a missile component (BEL, about INR4 crore per analyst) with execution in about three months.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: One assignment under way in Hyderabad, with a second data centre in Vizag. Management expects 7-8% of FY27 revenue and EBITDA of 14-15%; no long-term capex planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 60-70% expected, with order book of about INR7,150 crore to be executed over 18-20 months.
Net profit growth of about 60-70% in absolute terms (analyst reading: 50-60% on bottom line); management said margins should be maintained.
EBITDA margin for FY27 to be flat or up 20-30 bps; Q1 margins expected to hold since materials were procured in advance.
Target 1.5 GW of solar EPC commissioning in FY27 and 7.8 GW portfolio to be commissioned over 2-2.5 years.
Vision 2030: 25 GW of renewable capacity (16 GW solar, 9 GW BESS) and about USD 1 billion revenue.
Migration to main board of BSE and NSE planned in FY27.
capex_capacity: Integrated manufacturing plant on about 27 acres near Hyderabad: capex INR120-130 crore including land; construction to start in Q2 FY27 with about one-year build time; incremental revenue expected from FY28.

AP 2 GW IPP via SPV, with about INR9,000 crore order value excluded from the INR7,147 crore order book; phased build of 250 MW first, then 500 MW tranches, full 2 GW by 2030, revenue from 2031; first 250 MW needs about INR250 crore equity.
GreenBond RE Park IPP targets 2 GW; IPP IRR expected about 17-18% for solar and 12-13% for BESS BOO projects.
Adani EPC order (about INR1,050 crore) at about 20% completion with plant to be commissioned by March 2027; management said it is slightly ahead of schedule.
demand_pricing: Tender participation of INR25,000-30,000 crore with a 20-25% win rate; about INR2,850 crore of L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27.
Company stayed out of reverse auctions on some BESS tenders it considered unviable; it lost NTPC BESS tenders on price.
Receivable collections from NLC, NTPC, Singareni and MAHAGENCO with working capital of 85-90 days; PSU collection risk not seen.
Cable prices rose about 17-18% in the last quarter of FY26; steel also rose, with the increase seen as seasonal plus geopolitical. Some contracts are pass-through and some fixed.
Data-centre capex per MW of INR35-40 crore of company scope; starting size 2-3 MW, scalable to 10 MW.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 60-70% revenue growth on the INR7,150 crore order book, with profit growing about 60-70% in absolute terms; an analyst's reading of 50-60% for the bottom line was not corrected.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 margin dip and whether FY27 margin of 11-12% EBITDA and 7% PAT is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip was attributed to low-margin billing in Q4 and higher steel and cable costs; the CMD said 11-12% EBITDA and about 7% PAT were achievable comfortably.

qa_highlights.question: Equity needs and funding for the 2 GW AP IPP?
qa_highlights.answer: Phased equity of about INR250 crore for the first 250 MW; the rest to be raised in tranches. Management said it has funding avenues and no immediate QIP plan was stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the company not part of recent NTPC and Coal India BESS tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recent BESS tenders were largely unviable; it bid in some NTPC tenders but was not L1, and stopped at reverse-auction thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre margins and revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres are expected to be 7-8% of FY27 revenue at EBITDA of 14-15%; the company will not hold long-term capex and aims to hand over shells and infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Segmental services revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said O&M rose to about INR140 crore from INR90 crore and that some services had been reclassified into EPC; it said it would recheck the segment disclosure.

risks_watch: Segmental reporting inconsistency: services revenue figures in the quarterly disclosure were questioned and management committed to recheck.
Raw material inflation (steel, cables) and geopolitical effects on petroleum-linked inputs; Q1 FY27 margin guidance depends on procurement lock-in.
Working capital: current liabilities up sharply on TReDS and advances; receivables about 27-28% of revenue, aging 87 days, with some items over one year.
Execution risk: 1.5 GW commissioning target in FY27 and the Adani order commissioning by March 2027.
Funding and dilution for the 2 GW AP IPP and the AP BESS project financial closure, which was still pending.
Defence entry depends on trials of the missile component and on inorganic deals for three companies still in advanced talks.
Track L1 conversion of INR2,850 crore in Q1 FY27 and the Bryanston data-centre assignment.

543972|2026-03.headline: Aeroflex Q4 FY26 total income rose 38% YoY to INR126.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 23.86%; skid assemblies scaling to 15,000 units per annum.
543972|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 and FY26 performance, with Q4 total income of INR126.5 crore (+38% YoY), EBITDA of INR30 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR17.6 crore (+57%). FY26 total income was INR443.3 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR99.7 crore (+26%) and PAT INR55.5 crore. The new liquid cooling skid assemblies business contributed about 5% of FY26 sales, with 617 skids sold, and capacity is being lifted from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters. Management flagged design and customer quality-audit bottlenecks that delayed skid supply, and guided FY27 growth of about 35% with base business growth of 15-20%.

financial_highlights.change: Majority of sales in Q3 and Q4

segments.name: Liquid cooling skid assemblies
segments.commentary: 617 skids sold in FY26 for ~INR21.2 crore, all in India and supplied to one exclusive principal; ~5% of FY26 sales, guided to 20-22% of FY27 sales. Average selling price guided at INR3-3.25 lakh per skid.

segments.name: Hoses and assemblies (value-added)
segments.commentary: Value-added products (assemblies, fittings and bellows) were 52% of FY26 sales. Management said hose assemblies remain the core business for the next 2-3 years, with 75-80% of hose assembly sales from exports.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%; peak revenue potential about INR80 crore at ~85% utilisation. Targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years. Management called it the highest-margin product.

segments.name: Hyd-Air (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR31.64 crore; utilisation about 60%. Capacity to be used mainly for in-house fittings and connectors for Aeroflex's own projects.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic share rose to 31% of FY26 sales from 26%, with domestic sales up about 40% in Q4. Exports still about 60%; exports grew in double digits in Q4 per management. Largest international customer is 25-26% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total growth guided at about 35%, with base business growth of 15-20%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target around 23% (FY26 was 22.6%); around 25% over the next couple of years.
Skid assembly capacity to rise from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters.
Skid utilisation target of 60-70% by March 2027 (March closing month, not full-year average); peak utilisation 75-80%.

Some skid supply to international markets targeted within FY27; no finalised plan yet.
Expected sales from new data centre hose products (last-mile cooling, firefighting) from next quarter; annealing furnace due by end of 2026.
capex_capacity: Skid assemblies capacity scaled from 2,000 to 6,000 units per annum; expansion to 15,000 per annum targeted within about two quarters; management said further expansion beyond 15,000 is the ultimate aim but not the current focus.
Two robotic welding lines commissioned to improve automation and precision.
New annealing furnace targeted for commissioning by end of calendar 2026.
Miniature metal bellows capacity at 60,000 pieces; no further expansion planned this year, with capital redeployed to liquid cooling.
Hyd-Air utilisation about 60%, with plans to absorb in-house demand rather than add capex.
demand_pricing: Management said the liquid cooling TAM is about INR3 billion growing to about INR21 billion in 5-6 years (~34-35% CAGR), and liquid cooling is about 10-11% of data centre cost.
Skid supply is currently behind demand, with the principal's design work now done in-house and end-customer quality audits adding time; management expects smoothing over the next couple of months.
Orders for skids are visible only from the one exclusive principal; other customer talks have just begun.
Management said Aeroflex is among the only Indian skid manufacturers and competes more on supply than price; overseas landed-cost pricing for hoses is about 25-30% cheaper than local alternatives.
US tariffs: Section 232 tariff on products reduced from around mid-February; current rate cited as 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Order book for liquid cooling skids and planned utilisation for 15,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book not disclosed due to agreement; a full-year pipeline is shared by the principal and broken into quarterly POs. Peak utilisation 75-80%; target 60-70% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did skid execution lag last quarter's expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks are design finalisation (earlier done by principal, now in-house) and rigorous end-customer quality and welding audits, which management expects to ease over a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export share decline (from ~69% to ~60%) the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports rose in double digits in Q4; the ratio shifted because domestic sales grew about 40%. Skid sales will be domestic, so the domestic share will rise further.

qa_highlights.question: Metal bellows FY26 revenue, utilisation and path to scale?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%, ARR about INR12 crore; targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years, with sales cycles longer than other products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR40 crore income tax demand (AY 2018-19) a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand relates to a reopened assessment on a bank interest waiver from the company's takeover of a stressed entity. Management said disclosures were made and advisers are confident of reversal on appeal; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and ASP outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Skid margin is in line with company average (not disclosed separately). ASP guided INR3-3.25 lakh per skid versus about INR3.4 lakh cited by an analyst for FY26.

543972|2026-06.headline: Aeroflex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72.4% YoY to INR145.97 crore, with EBITDA margin at 23.04% and SFN skid assemblies contributing INR32.4 crore (~23%).
543972|2026-06.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR145.97 crore (+72.4% YoY), with EBITDA up 116% to INR33.5 crore and margin up 468 bps to 23.04%. PAT rose 162% to INR18.79 crore (about 13% margin). Growth came from flexible hoses (+41% YoY), assemblies and value-added products (faster), and the new SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies for data centres. Management said sequential margin dipped due to ramp-up manpower costs for Taloja and Chakan facilities and West Asia-related logistics costs.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.4 crore on 1,040 units in Q1, about 23% of revenue. Capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/yr; target 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27. Management says skid margin is in line with company average.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR3 crore in Q1. Management expects an uptick over the next two quarters; bellows utilisation is not yet at optimum.

segments.name: Hyd-Air
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR7 crore in Q1. Used internally for hose-assembly components, not sold to third parties; capex plan under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SFN average price per skid decline?

543972|2026-09.headline: Aeroflex Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR200 crores for the first time, with total income of INR207.68 crores, up 87% YoY, and PAT of INR36.56 crores.

The company changed depreciation from WDV to SLM from 1 April 2026, reducing depreciation by INR8.41 crores in both Q2 and H1. It also announced a total capex of INR202 crores for capacity expansion and the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering into Aeroflex.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quarterly EEI growth trajectory continue, and what about AI/data-centre traction in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is almost comparable to last year's Q4 and the company wants to beat guidance rather than raise it, citing seasonality in Europe and Diwali. Data-centre wins are one announced plus 3-4 more, with about 10 quotes outstanding; domestic bookings were about 20% higher YoY but billing lagged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Lumel S.A. and India growth came from the German customer and from solar inverters?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EUR5 mn German order is already executed; the EUR3 mn follow-on runs to year-end, estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales. Solar is under 5% of total, about INR8-9 crore last year, targeted at INR24-25 crore this year and INR250-300 crore next year; EEI contribution margin for solar and EMS is 15-20% versus about 45% average.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and adjacencies: CT capacity, PCB/EMS, battery systems and M&A size?
qa_highlights.answer: CT capacity is moving from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage to follow. Three SMT lines run PCB/EMS, with a fourth once they hit three shifts. Battery systems will be indirect via hybrid inverters. Acquisitions considered in the INR50-200 crore range; about 4-5 targets under review, none at a serious stage.

risks_watch: EEI growth sustainability: management held guidance at about 20% top line and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite 34% Q1 growth; watch whether Q2-Q4 deliver and whether seasonality (European summer and winter holidays, Diwali) bites.
Lumel Alucast: still EBITDA-negative (-6.4% adjusted) with revenue down 41.2%; breakeven targeted by end FY27 and double-digit margin in about 2 years depends on RFQ conversion and a 6-month ramp.
Domestic billing lag: bookings about 20% above last year but billing has not caught up, leaving a backlog to work off.
Customer concentration: one German grid-upgrade customer is estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales, with the EUR3 mn follow-on running only to year-end.

Solar scale-up risk: FY27 target of INR24-25 crore and next-year INR250-300 crore depends on iNEO 3-phase up to 12 kW and 50 kW models due by end FY27, plus hybrid inverters still in development; pricing is competitive with Chinese imports.
Margin and PAT pressure: consolidated PAT fell 1.4% YoY on a INR20 mn rise in depreciation, and ESOP/SAR costs of INR20 mn per quarter continue for about three more years.
key_quotes: So we see the growth coming out of multiple factors actually.
And this quarter, we have delivered more than that on the EEI business. And it will be around that or more throughout the year.
We want to keep our guidelines, which are already kind of aggressive, and we want to beat them by performance rather than giving guidelines which are a bit risky.
So any addition to the top line will very quickly reflect into the bottom line.
We're almost doubling our capacity, close to doubling our capacity.
543977|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on EEI and Lumel S.A., with management repeatedly describing growth as broad-based and sustainable. Noticeably cautious on guidance, declining to raise the 20% top-line target and saying it prefers to beat guidance rather than give aggressive numbers. Lumel Alucast and US timelines were framed as a process needing time, and several answers on inorganic plans and forward numbers were deliberately non-committal.

rows.why: Nashik facility is partially commissioned with both buildings complete and full completion in 1-2 months, and CT capacity is being lifted from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 units/day with machinery already ordered.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic order bookings were about 20% above last year, US target is INR45 crore this year versus about INR30 crore last year, and solar is targeted at INR24-25 crore from under 5% of total, though consolidated revenue grew only 4.2% in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: US business scale-up to INR45 crore this year
rows.why: US revenue rose from about INR20 crore to INR30 crore last year, with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years, supported by more sales staff and Mexico/Canada focus.

rows.label: Lumel Alucast RFQ conversion and return to growth
rows.why: RFQs are in advanced commercial negotiation, ramp-up takes about 6 months after award, and revenue is down 41.2% to INR443 mn, so breakeven by end FY27 depends on conversion.

543978|2026-03.headline: Ratnaveer guides FY27 top line of ~1,350-1,500 crore and FY28 consolidated 2,500 crore incl. 750 crore from new CCL plant; FY26 standalone OCF negative ~48 crore.
543978|2026-03.overview: Management reiterated a growth plan built around a new copper-clad laminate (CCL) plant in Gujarat, with first line targeted for November 2026 production and five lines over about two years. FY26 top line was 1,078 crore against a 1,350 crore target for the current year, with stainless/fastener business guided at about 25% CAGR. Cash flow questions drew a contested answer: an analyst cited FY26 standalone operating cash flow of about negative 48 crore, while management attributed the low cash generation to capex advances, depreciation and QIP funds held as FDs. Receivables rose sharply (analyst cited about 65 crore to 175 crore), which management attributed to new product launches and longer credit to new customers.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue grew from 419 crore three years earlier

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 standalone operating cash flow (analyst-cited, disputed in detail)

financial_highlights.change: Mgmt said partly reclassified from finance cost
Falls to about 42-43% after 330 crore QIP

segments.name: Stainless steel fasteners and washers (existing business)
segments.commentary: Management guided 25% CAGR, with 1,350 crore target for the current year and about 1,800 crore in three years. Company claims largest SKU count for stainless washers in India and serves 31 countries.

segments.name: Copper-clad laminate (CCL, new)
segments.commentary: Five-line plant with 338 crore ECMS approval; first line targeted November 2026. Individual CCL business guided at about 20% EBITDA and 13% PAT, with 750 crore revenue at 69% utilisation targeted for FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line: management said 1,350-1,400 crore is the base case, and that it remains on track for about 1,500 crore after an analyst flagged a downgrade from earlier 1,500 crore guidance.
FY28 consolidated target of about 2,500 crore revenue, 13-13.5% EBITDA and about 10.5% PAT, including 750 crore from CCL.
CCL first line production targeted November 2026; machine dispatch from China around July 2026; installation August-October 2026.
Remaining four CCL lines to be installed over the next two years depending on first-line performance; utilisation of 80-85% targeted by 2028, with 69% assumed conservatively.
Expected PLI and state incentives (about 50% of capex from central and state schemes, power cost exemption, interest subsidy) cited, with disbursement in about 4-5 months after project completion.
Planned 330 crore fundraise (QIP or equivalent) targeted for completion by September 2026; remaining warrant balance to be converted by about September 2027.
Proposed acquisition of a European precision components company: management said due diligence will take about 10-12 more months.
capex_capacity: CCL plant: 5 lines in total under ECMS (338 crore approval); project cost about 351 crore plus about 46 crore solar; split about 70% plant and machinery (turnkey), 80% building, and 12% miscellaneous (as stated).
Machinery ordered from a Chinese technology partner; advance paid January 2026 and second tranche paid; second-round inspection completed; civil and PV work in progress.
Technology agreement signed December 2025; partner to supply machinery, install, train staff and provide 1.5-2 years of quality support. Management said no royalty is payable.
Plant is in Gujarat; land already owned by the company.
Capex 1, Capex 2 and Capex 2A referenced as ongoing for the existing business.
demand_pricing: Management claims no anti-dumping duty currently on CCL imports and states 10-13% price competitiveness versus imports; Indian PCB makers receive 2% cash subsidy for buying indigenous material (as stated).
Management says the five lines would be about 2% of Indian CCL demand, which it says is growing 30-35% (or 35-40% CAGR per another comment).
Soft confirmations received from PCB companies; no firm pre-orders yet. Management said one or two customers may be ready to buy the first line.
Management said the Iran war (about 45-60 days) has not affected demand; oil and gas and consumable costs rising, and management said these can be passed on to customers.
Customer concentration: top 5 washer customers about 2-5% of sales; top finishing-line customers about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the warrants at 159 due for conversion and will they be forfeited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% was already paid, the balance can be converted, and the 18-month window runs to about September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for CCL, technical tie-up terms and competition from China and Korea?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner is paid through machinery purchase, with no royalty; the plant is fully automated and it claims 10-13% price advantage versus imports.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated FY28 2,500 crore plan and FY26 revenue base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1,078 crore in FY26 and 1,350 crore target this year, with the existing business growing 25% CAGR to 1,800 crore and CCL adding 750 crore in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Negative operating cash flow and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Ajay Panchal said net cash flow of 203 crore was inflated by QIP funds held as FDs, and that advances to capex suppliers and depreciation drove the weak FY26 operating cash flow; the analyst's 48 crore figure was not directly rebutted.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rising from 65 crore to about 175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables rose on new products, new customers and launch credit, and expects normalisation as the business matures; no quantified timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: PLI incentive quantum and timing on 70 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of eligible capex (25% central plus 25% state) would be reimbursed, received within about 3-6 months of completion, and power, logistics and interest subsidies also apply.

risks_watch: CCL execution: Chinese machinery arrival around July 2026, monsoon impact on civil works, and first production target November 2026.
Funding gap: 330 crore raise targeted by September 2026 to fund CCL project and working capital; execution risk on fundraise timing.
Cash flow and receivables: negative operating cash flow reported by analyst for FY26, and receivables growth well above revenue growth.
Warrant conversion and dilution: promoter stake may fall from about 47-48% to 42-43% after QIP and warrants.
Management statements on CCL demand (soft confirmations only, no firm orders) and the European acquisition (10-12 months to close) are unverified.
Some management answers were unclear or inconsistent (e.g., CCL CAGR quoted as both 30-35% and 35-40%; guidance changed between 1,350 and 1,500 crore for FY27).
543978|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the CCL opportunity and growth targets, but evasive on cash flow and receivables, and inconsistent on several figures and guidance numbers.
key_quotes: So, we have been tied up with the Chinese company for the technological partner, and tail up to the installation, commissioning, and quality of the product should be coming out.
Total, we are getting the 338 crores of the approval from the ECMS scheme of Central Government of India.
No, dear. Sanjay, there is no, royalty would be that, but yes, we have an internal agreement that we have been buying the machine from them.
So, in 2028, we can definitely give the full utilization of this plant. So, the 750 crores would be a definitely achievable figure.

rows.why: Management guided 4 further CCL lines over two years and a 330 crore fundraise by Sept 2026 to fund the project; existing-business utilisation is not disclosed, but CCL line 1 utilisation is targeted at 80-85% by 2028, which implies follow-on capex.

rows.why: Management is holding FY27 at 1,350-1,500 crore against FY26 revenue of 1,078 crore, with no evidence yet of pre-orders for CCL (soft confirmations only).

rows.why: Receivables reportedly rose from about 65 crore to 175 crore and FY26 standalone OCF was about negative 48 crore (analyst-cited, not rebutted), with management giving no quantified timeline for normalisation.

543980|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15.1% to INR387.8 crores and FY26 total income reached INR1,499.8 crores, with Dombivli opened ahead of schedule.
543980|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR387.8 crores (up 15.1%), EBITDA of INR89.2 crores (23% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crores (up 11.5%). For FY26, total income was INR1,499.8 crores (up 15.2%), EBITDA INR343.3 crores (up 14.4%, 22.9% margin) and PAT INR194.2 crores. Dombivli, the first greenfield hospital since listing, was inaugurated in February 2026, about two months before the call. Management outlined a pipeline taking capacity from about 1,200 to nearly 3,000 beds, including a 400-bed BKC hospital, with funding planned from internal accruals and debt capped at 3x EBITDA.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 75%; growth expected to be inflation-linked at current capacity, with an expansion awaiting final approvals.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy close to 65% with headroom to grow; Pune South is on track to open in calendar 2028.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy 45-50% after last year's added capacity; ramp-up driven by occupancy and case mix; second phase of 111 beds to be triggered when occupancy nears 60%.

segments.name: Dombivli (new, greenfield)
segments.commentary: Opened February 2026 with 750,000 sq ft built, 500-bed superstructure and about 300 beds fitted out; expected EBITDA burn INR2-3 crores per month on average in FY27, with breakeven targeted by end of calendar 2027/2028; INR9.4 crores Dombivli contribution is included in Q4 results.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year; EBITDA breakeven expected at end of two years of operation (calendar 2027-28).
Dombivli insurance tie-ups expected in 6-12 months, linked to NABH accreditation that needs about six months of operating data.
Pune South to open in calendar 2028; Mira Road expected to start excavation by end of calendar 2026.
Thane expansion approvals expected in FY27; scope and scale to be disclosed once final approvals are received.
Land payment for BKC: 25% of land cost paid; management said the remainder would be paid within this financial year.
Capacity target of about 1,700 new beds in this cycle, taking long-term capacity to nearly 3,000 beds at an average capex of about INR1.5 crores per bed.
Funding: internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt capped at 3x EBITDA considered sufficient; detailed calculations to follow.
Base business growth: Thane inflation-linked; Pune inflation plus occupancy; Indore occupancy, inflation and case mix. Management declined to quantify growth given inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Dombivli opened February 2026, ahead of the Q1 FY27 target, on time and on budget with no cost escalation.
BKC: 400-bed quaternary care hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft in BKC; land allotted by MMRDA, with regulatory clearance and possession formalities underway.
Mira Road: architectural drawings complete, regulatory clearances in progress, excavation expected by end of calendar 2026.
Pune South on track for calendar 2028 opening; all projects are greenfield, full-scale hubs in Mumbai and Pune on owned real estate.
Indore phase two (111 beds) on hold until occupancy reaches around 60%.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 11.7% YoY to INR67,700 in Q4; drivers cited were Indore case-mix maturity and insurance renewals (roughly every two years) giving price increases plus inflation.
Insurance is 55.4% of revenue; government 1%. Insurance renewals are rolling with no single season.
International medical tourism is very small; management said it is not a focus and is not margin accretive, preferring domestic and local demand within a 45-minute drive radius.
Cost watch items: depreciating rupee and capex cost inflation; doctor costs and consumables not yet materially impacted by global supply chain disruption.
Management referred to a current war situation as a factor limiting inflation visibility.

qa_highlights.question: How is Dombivli ramping in occupancy and revenue, and when will the major insurance tie-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about two months of operations, so occupancy is too early to quantify; insurance tie-ups are linked to NABH accreditation and are likely in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and funding for the expansion to about 2,900 beds be managed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals over the next 5 years plus some debt, with a self-imposed ceiling of 3x EBITDA, should cover it.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy and ARPOB by unit, and can the base business grow more than 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Thane about 75% occupancy, Pune close to 65%, Indore 45-50%. Growth is inflation-linked plus occupancy and case mix; no numeric guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ARPOB increase during the year?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of Indore maturing with better case mix, and insurance renewals after a two-year cycle giving price increases plus inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dombivli add fixed costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, more fixed costs are expected as doctor hiring continues over the next couple of years for a large facility.

qa_highlights.question: Share of revenue from foreign patients and the government's medical tourism push?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little foreign revenue; management is not focused on international medical tourism and does not see it as margin accretive.

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month and rising fixed costs until breakeven; insurance empanelment and NABH accreditation timing.
Funding load from BKC and the wider pipeline (about 1,700 beds, average INR1.5 crores per bed); rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation.
Indore: occupancy still 45-50%, and the second phase depends on occupancy reaching about 60%.
Regulatory approvals for Thane expansion and BKC/Mira Road site clearances (MMRDA possession formalities) remain pending, with no firm dates.
Insurance renewals rolling through the year, with the 55.4% insurance mix exposing the business to tariff negotiations.
Management declined to guide base business growth beyond inflation-linked, citing war-related inflation uncertainty.
543980|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on delivery, citing Dombivli opening early and on budget, but cautious on macro, declining to quantify inflation or base-business growth and deferring capex and occupancy numbers until more data is available.
key_quotes: We set ourselves a target of commissioning it by Q1 FY27, and I'm very pleased that we beat that and opened ahead of schedule.
We are not trying to just grow fast. We are trying to grow right.
This is an asset-heavy model by deliberate choice.
I don't want to take a guess of how inflation will play out.

rows.why: Dombivli EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month in FY27 with rising fixed costs, insurance tie-ups not expected until 6-12 months out, and rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation are the main risks to the plan.

rows.why: Management said insurance tie-ups are likely in 6-12 months and linked to NABH accreditation, which needs about six months of operating data from the February 2026 opening, and insurance is 55.4% of revenue.

rows.label: BKC land payment and 400-bed approval
rows.why: 25% of BKC land cost is paid and management said the remainder will be paid within this financial year, with MMRDA land allotted and clearances underway for the 400-bed hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft.

rows.why: Gross debt is about INR500 crores against cash of about INR545 crores (net cash positive) at March 2026, and funding of the ~1,700-bed pipeline relies on internal accruals plus debt under a self-imposed 3x EBITDA ceiling, with detailed calculations still to come.

543980|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores at 19.3% margin, PAT INR37.5 crores; Dombivli drag INR9.5 crores.
543980|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter of operations for Dombivli Hospital, which contributed a INR9.5 crore EBITDA drag, in line with management's expectations. Consolidated total income was INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores (19.3% margin) and PAT INR37.5 crores. ARPOB rose to INR73,500 and ALOS was 3.76 days, with average occupancy at 59.6% diluted by the expanded Dombivli bed base. Management kept Dombivli's guidance (EBITDA loss of INR2-3 crores per month on operating beds, breakeven in roughly 1.5-2 years) unchanged and confirmed the Indore expansion and a backward-integration IV fluids acquisition.

financial_highlights.value: approx. zero; roughly INR500 crores debt and INR500 crores cash (approximate, per management)

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy stuck at mid-70s (about 75%); growth expected to track inflationary pricing with limited occupancy upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy in low-to-mid 60s; management expects growth to plateau or slow in percentage terms as the remaining ~15% occupancy headroom is filled, with pricing as a further driver.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 50%; revenue up about 10% YoY but EBITDA margin about 12% on new team buildup and doctor hires (a couple of crores of added cost). Expected to grow faster than Thane and Pune as occupancy improves.

segments.name: Dombivli
segments.commentary: First full quarter; occupancy roughly 25-30%; operating on about 200 beds with a further ~300 beds upcoming; fixed cost about INR6-7 crores per month; EBITDA loss guidance INR2-3 crores per month; oncology (radiation/LINAC) expected by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli EBITDA loss guidance of INR2-3 crores per month on currently operating beds retained; EBITDA breakeven guided at 1.5-2 years, with management saying the second year should be the breakeven year.
ARPOB expected to grow at inflation for mature units and above inflation for new units for a few years as case mix improves.

Ramp-up model: initial EBITDA drag for the first 1-2 years per hospital; after reaching about 60% occupancy on installed beds, capacity is added to bring occupancy back to about 40%, with some margin compression but no EBITDA loss.
Board-imposed debt ceiling of 3x EBITDA; current capex expected to be funded by internal accruals and cash, with debt possibly needed toward the end of the cycle.
Five-year visibility: all three announced projects to be delivered within five years; focus on Western India.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 margin guidance beyond the Dombivli inputs.
capex_capacity: Three upcoming projects on track; line of sight to around 3,000 beds with the growing footprint.
Dombivli operating on about 200 beds, with about 300 more beds to be commissioned.
Indore being readied for the next phase of expansion.
IV fluids manufacturing line acquired as backward integration for the pharmacy subsidiary, costing about INR35-40 crores including infrastructure; management says it is not a shift into pharma.
Management described the BKC hospital as a new site ~100 m from the bullet train station.
demand_pricing: ARPOB growth of about 10% in the quarter, driven by a combination of case-mix improvement and insurance contract renegotiations.
Dombivli payer mix mostly self-paid; insurance empanelment (cashless) still pending and expected to reduce friction and lift occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the other income jump a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not call it a normal run rate; a weaker dollar boosted gains for this export-heavy company and is part of business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9.9% Wires & Cables margin driven by inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there was no inventory gain or loss; improvement is organic from scale, absorption and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the implied pricing growth from metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated ~40% net metal price impact translating to ~25% overall product pricing, after earlier ~30% LME estimate for Q2 versus prior-year Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why do domestic and export margins differ across wires and cables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a consumer brand product in India earning premium margins, while export cables need precision and approvals; domestic cable margin is 6-7% and expected to reach 10-11% at scale.

543984|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose to INR 1,279 crore with 12.3% revenue growth; net debt/EBITDA ~3x (3.07x) and FY27 revenue guided at 10-11%.
543984|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue growth was 12.3% against a 9-11% guidance band, with same-store RevPAR up 9.5%, despite several one-off disruptions that cut revenue by an estimated INR 45-52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 8.8% to INR 463 crore at a 36.2% margin, and the GST slab change weighed on H2 margins. Q4 EBITDA fell 6% YoY to about INR 120 crore, which management attributes to GST, FF&E charges, pre-opening costs and the Middle East conflict hitting March revenue. Net debt fell to INR 1,450 crore after the GIC infusion, and a deferred tax credit of about INR 330 crore lifted reported PAT to about INR 567 crore. Management guided FY27 same-store revenue growth of 9-10% and total revenue growth of 10-11%, and a 38%-plus group margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?

Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?

Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: March revenue fell below -1% YoY and the effect is still continuing into April; management says it may keep affecting Q1 FY27 absolute numbers.

543984|2026-06.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.
543984|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 7.3% YoY to Rs 308.3 crore reported, or 10.8% on a comparable basis after excluding Rs 9.3 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base. Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

financial_highlights.change: down about 4% YoY reported; comparable margin about 12.1%

unchanged since last upgrade in FY26

segments.commentary: Occupancy 78.4% in Q1 with RevPAR growth below mid-scale; management says the raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across all segments.

segments.name: Mid-scale portfolio
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.name: RARE India (asset-light leisure)
segments.commentary: 75 hotels, 1,046 rooms across 15 states; management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years, against about Rs 47 crore invested to date.

segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.
capex_capacity: Seven new hotels in the committed pipeline total 1,660 rooms, mostly upper upscale and upscale; about 450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

risks_watch: Rate softness from lower international inbound mix: rate growth is expected to recover only in H2 FY27, and July's split is one month of data.

543985|2026-03.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.
543985|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results, with standalone revenue of about INR1,853 crores (up 42%) and PAT of about INR133 crores (up 52%). Q4 standalone revenue was about INR593 crores (up 44%) with reported EBITDA of about INR55 crores. The DICE acquisition was restructured from a 100% share purchase (originally INR123 crores) to an asset purchase for about INR68 crores excluding GST, which moves its costs onto the standalone P&L. Management withheld EBITDA guidance until integration completes, and cash flow is now the top priority, with operating cash flow about minus INR6 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Zaggle core (Save, Propel, Zoyer)
segments.commentary: Program fees were about 41% of revenue and SaaS about 2% in FY26. Zoyer and BROME drove a significant rise in interchange fees. Management is deliberately reducing redemption-led Propel models that absorb cash, and expects Propel margin to recover toward about 5.5% from about 4% in Q4.

segments.name: 86400 (formerly Mobileware)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR34 crores in FY25 to about INR74 crores in FY26 (up 118%). EBITDA rose from about INR5.4 crores to about INR18 crores and PAT from about INR1.6 crores to INR11 crores, driven by UPI volumes and new bank partners.

segments.name: GreenEdge
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR36.5 crores in FY25 to about INR103.7 crores in FY26 (up about 184%). EBITDA rose from about INR3.4 crores to about INR11 crores and PAT from INR2.1 crores to about INR8.1 crores. Standalone revenue growth of 40-50% is projected for FY27.

segments.name: Zagg.money (formerly Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: New acquisition for retail credit cards on UPI and TPAP. Management reports an annualised run rate of about 36,000-40,000 new cards, with a base of about 25,000 cardholders. Revenue is referral fees and interchange share with no balance-sheet risk.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Management said performance was unsatisfactory last year. Rebranding and a Tax AI copilot launch are planned for Q2 FY27, and Quesscorp partnership covers a base of 5 lakh-plus users.

segments.name: DICE (asset purchase)
segments.commentary: Acquired as a spend management suite, IP and enterprise contracts for about INR68 crores excluding GST, against an original INR123 crores share-purchase valuation. DICE was loss-making in FY25 and likely in FY26; FY25 revenue was about INR10 crores, with FY26 described as significantly higher. Around 100-plus team members join.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at about 25-30%; consolidated growth at about 40%.
EBITDA guidance deferred to 'the next few months' until DICE integration completes, since DICE costs now sit on the standalone P&L.

Management says the 2026 credit card business is growing faster than initial expectations, with card acquisition the lead indicator before spend-led revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capitalised development costs nearly doubled, and does free cash flow better reflect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only new product development is capitalised, not maintenance, and it will track operating and free cash flow more closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Propel margins fall from about 10% to 4% YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the full-year margin of about 6% and said it is exiting redemption-heavy Propel models that absorb cash, sacrificing some margin; it expects about 5.5% in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 standalone growth guided at 25-30% after 42% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the much larger base (about 5-6x since IPO) and a deliberate cash-flow focus that may slow Propel Points growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR40 crores to INR129 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split receivables by business, said the net receivable position was negative about INR33-34 crores at end-September and is now close to breakeven, and cited trade receivables as one cash lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated operating cash flow about minus INR52 crores versus about minus INR6 crores standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiaries are nascent businesses recently acquired, with investments made and efficiency gains to come.

qa_highlights.question: Does DICE dilute the EBITDA run rate and the 11-12% margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DICE's impact is no worse than originally envisaged, with costs now on standalone P&L; it was loss-making and EBITDA guidance will follow integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Propel worth keeping given its low net revenue and working-capital use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Propel is a feeder for cross-sell and stickiness, about 90% of spend sits in program fees, and cash and ROCE optimisation is under way.

DICE integration may lift employee and other costs in the next quarter, with EBITDA guidance still pending.

Overseas expansion (UAE and US) is delayed by regional conflict; the US launch slipped to FY27 year-end, and the company has no on-ground presence in the Middle East.
CFO role is interim after Aditya Kumar Grandhi's departure; a permanent CFO is expected soon.
Discrepancies in call figures (for example standalone FY26 EBITDA of INR181 vs INR183 crores and a GreenEdge growth percentage correction) should be checked against the filed results.

543985|2026-06.headline: Zaggle Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR423 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 10.1% on DICE costs and expensed capitalisation.
543985|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to about INR423 crore, while stand-alone revenue grew 18% to about INR390 crore against a soft seasonal Q1. Adjusted EBITDA was about INR34.7 crore (8.2% margin vs 10.1% a year ago), pressured by DICE integration and relocation costs (about INR3 crore in the last two months of the quarter, before any DICE revenue), one-time expenses, a moderation of capitalisation, annual increments and Zagg.Money costs. Management said DICE revenue starts from July 1 (Q2 FY27), reiterated the 40% consolidated growth guidance and a 25% stand-alone target, and pivoted the stated focus to cash flow and calibrated capitalisation. Analysts pressed on the sharp growth slowdown, margin volatility and the lack of explicit EBITDA guidance.

segments.name: Propel
segments.commentary: Consolidated Propel margin 7.1%, stand-alone about 5%, including spillover of overriding commissions realised in Q1. Signed Saint Gobain, Supreme Pipes and Phoenix India during the quarter.

segments.commentary: Transactions up 43% YoY and transaction value up 5.8% YoY; annualised spend run-rate about INR100 crore. First contract with an OMC (HPCL, 5-year aggregator agreement for DT Plus).

segments.name: Zagg.Money (Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: Annualised new card acquisition run-rate raised to about 84,000 from 36,000 a quarter earlier; management cited about INR2.5 crore loss on the business. Co-brand launches with PNB and AU Small Finance Bank.

segments.name: DICE (acquired, spend management)
segments.commentary: Acquired as asset purchase for about INR68 crore excl. GST (from INR123 crore initial valuation). About 100 staff relocated from Pune to Hyderabad; revenue from novated contracts only from Q2 FY27. FY26 DICE revenue about INR12 crore; FY27 target INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (rebranding to Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR80 lakh, +65% YoY; B2B business expected to grow about 120%. Management says on track to breakeven this financial year.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore invested in Unobanc (moneyHOP), which holds an RBI Authorised Dealer Category-II licence for cross-border payments and forex cards.

No explicit EBITDA margin guidance; management said it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 14-15% framed over 5-7 years.

Management moved some high working-capital banks' customers to other banks to prioritise cash flow, which slows program fees. Management said it is not moving away from the 40% consolidated guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin is about 8.2% and it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. About INR3 crore of DICE cost came in over the last two months of Q1 with no revenue, since revenue starts July 1.

qa_highlights.question: What were the expensed items that were previously capitalised, and why are they only partly expensed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no selective capitalisation; the company is moving toward expensing more over time, subject to auditor agreement. One immediate client-required product cost about INR6 crore was fully expensed in Q1, and some infra and product development costs are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Has DICE payment-rail integration been completed and will payments revenue come from DICE from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority of integration is done; the last part is due by August 31 or at latest September 10. Management said payments-related DICE revenue from Q3 is certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is revenue per customer, and what is the program fee growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue per customer is about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore over about 4,000 customers). Management called the roughly 10% program fee growth 'by design' and said it expects improvement in coming months, with cash flow and calibrated capitalisation prioritised over the program fee number.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 13-15% EBITDA margin target still stand, and when will margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins have been in the 9-10% range for the last eight quarters and the 14-15% target is a 5-7 year aspiration. Cash flow turnaround to positive would take about 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: When will AI become a meaningful revenue driver, and what is the DICE revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal AI use helped cut about 12.5% of the FY26 cost base and reduced feature launch timelines by up to 50%. DICE FY26 revenue was about INR12 crore; FY27 target is INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

543988|2026-03.headline: Nuvama FY26 operating PAT crossed INR1,000 crore; Q4 operating PAT up 5% YoY to INR269 crore, with wealth and asset services driving growth.
543988|2026-03.overview: Management reported a growth year despite a volatile FY26 marked by tariffs, the West Asia crisis and subdued capital markets. Wealth and Private grew operating PBT by about 22-24%, and asset services recovered after a Q1 decline to end FY26 with revenue up about 12%. Capital markets (IB and IE) softened, with QIP volumes down and ECM subdued in Q4. Q4 firm revenue was about INR825 crore (+7% YoY; +13% excluding IE and IB), and firm ROE was 28%. Management says Wealth and Private now contribute 55% of firm revenue, and wealth, asset management and asset services together about 80%.

segments.name: Nuvama Private
segments.commentary: ARR assets about INR54,000 crore; ARR yield 1.00% in Q4, with management guiding an average of 90-95 bps. Lending is 10-12% of revenue. RM headcount rose from 90 to about 150 over four years. Operating PBT +24%.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Management fee income +31% YoY. Commercial real estate fund about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4, with the fund fully closed at about INR4,000 crore. Crossover 4 PE fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Private credit first fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Public markets roughly flat net flows.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR209 crore, above Q1 INR193 crore. FY26 revenue +12%, profit about +14-15%. Domestic RTA and trusteeship services expected live by mid-Q3 FY27. Global-local custodian tie-up on the verge of signing. Market share about 22% of chosen segments.

qa_highlights.question: How should ECM revenue share be modelled for FY27 given large upcoming IPOs, and what is the impact of the MF commission cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 40-45 live ECM and advisory mandates, and Q4 deal slippage is expected to recover. MF commission cut impact is hardly material, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and net margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: Is the asset services yield at risk as rates fall, and what drove the higher cash share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields should hold, as rate cuts have already flowed through. The cash share rose after a large client was replaced by many smaller clients; the portfolio mix is about 70:30 to 75:25. A rate hike would lift yields as deposits reprice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% wealth productivity gain from AI or from mix, and how do clients per RM evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to RM seasoning (under-one-year share fell to about 33%) plus AI tools. Net new money is the outcome, not the cause of productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for transactional revenue in FY27 and the insurance commission trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Transactional revenue is mostly broking and fixed income, which are insulated from geopolitics. Insurance yields are steady, with some first-year commission support from category 2 products.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income ratios evolve in Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth CTI fell 130-150 bps this year. Management guides about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with reinvestment in RM capacity as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 asset management flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PE Crossover 4 targets INR1,000-1,500 crore; private credit first fund INR1,000-1,500 crore with about half this year; CRE fund INR3,000-4,000 crore with 30-40% this year. SIF flow numbers to be discussed next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the Ultra-HNI book sits above INR10 crore, and what is the mix of wealth clients by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: Families above INR10 crore are about one-third of the total and contribute 70-75% of AUM. Tier 2 and beyond is 35-40% of Nuvama Wealth. Private: top 8 cities about 80-85%.

543988|2026-06.headline: Nuvama Q1 FY27 record quarter: revenue INR909 crores (+18% YoY) and operating PAT INR306 crores (+16% YoY), with client assets at INR5.36 lakh crores.

Client assets crossed INR5 lakh crores, and MPIS plus ARR assets together crossed INR1 lakh crores. rows.why: Management guided the new-state entry to Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with Pune named and Kerala explored, but no store count or capex was given.

rows.label: KLM Fashion Mall Telangana store closure and inventory transfer
rows.why: One KLM store is being closed (store count 19 to 18) with inventory and staff moved to other KLM and upcoming stores, after sustained degrowth.

rows.label: Valli Silks (Varamahalakshmi) expansion pause
