rows.why: New Valli stores of 3,000-4,000 sq ft are paused due to higher rent-to-revenue, with the next wave planned from Q4 FY27 or FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on full-year 12-15% guidance, store additions and the Karnataka growth push, but defensive and cautious on Q1 SSSG, rainfall and Q2-Q3 demand; analysts probed how the H2 SSSG recovery to +2-3% would come about and how much KLM and Telangana were dragging.

543990|2026-03.headline: FY26 presales of INR82.5bn and record PAT of about INR11bn-plus (exceptional RMZ gain); net debt near zero; FY27 launches guided above INR150bn.
543990|2026-03.overview: FY26 presales were about INR82.5bn, down year-on-year from FY25 but up over 30% annually on a FY22-FY26 view, with sales spread steadily across four quarters. Realisation per sq ft crossed INR15,000, up about 20% year-on-year, driven by price escalation and a mix shift to group housing. PAT reached an all-time high, helped by an exceptional item from the RMZ commercial joint venture, while net debt fell to roughly INR2bn. Management guided FY27 to new launches above INR150bn, presales above INR100bn, revenue recognition and collections of about INR50bn each.

financial_highlights.value: INR82.5bn (over 5 million sq ft, about 2,100 units)
financial_highlights.change: Down vs FY25 (FY25 was about INR100bn); up over 30% YoY on FY22-FY26 trend

financial_highlights.value: About INR26bn (about 3.75 million sq ft completed at INR6,800-6,900/sq ft)
About INR1,100-plus crore, including exceptional item from RMZ transaction

financial_highlights.change: Down to historical low per management

financial_highlights.value: About INR40bn; total cash collection incl. INR12.5bn JV receipt about INR52-53bn
financial_highlights.change: Marginal dip YoY; 30%+ CAGR over 3-4 years

segments.name: Residential (Gurugram / Sohna / Manesar)
segments.commentary: FY26 launches of about 6.5 million sq ft, with Cloverdale (about 1.75 million sq ft, Sector 71) and Signature Global Sarvam (about 3.75 million sq ft, Sector 37D) making up about 85%. Launches above INR10,000 crore saw sales above INR4,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial / JV with RMZ
segments.commentary: 50-50 JV for a mixed-use project in Sector 71 on the Southern Peripheral Road: about 5.5 million sq ft, with 4-4.5 million sq ft of office; expected capital value above INR150bn. Land is fully licensed and activation is planned in FY27.

guidance_outlook: New launches above INR150bn in FY27: about 2 million sq ft Tonino Lamborghini branded residence in Q1, a similar-sized Sector 71 launch in late Q2 or Q3, and a third launch in Q4 tied to the RMZ trade.
Presales above INR100bn in FY27, targeting about 40% sell-through on launch value (about INR60bn from new launches) with the rest from sustaining sales and inventory.
FY27 revenue recognition target of about INR50bn, implying completions of INR60-65bn; collections target above INR50bn.
Completion of about 12 million sq ft in the next 4-5 quarters, taking completed and delivered area to about 30 million sq ft.
Net debt near zero; FY27 land and BD focus on Sohna and larger-format plotted land parcels, with deals hoped to close in H1 FY27.

Expected FY27 capex in the RMZ JV of INR3,500-4,000 crore over 4-4.5 years, funded by JV debt and equity from both partners; Company-level share about INR1,500-2,000 crore per analyst arithmetic. Sanjeev Sharma said JV debt will not enter consolidated debt, but equity contributions will show as investment.
capex_capacity: Total land and development portfolio of about 40 million sq ft (21 million sq ft launched over 8 quarters plus 19 million sq ft land bank), GDV above INR70,000 crore; about 14.5 million sq ft to be executed solely and 5.5 million sq ft via RMZ JV.
About 18 million sq ft completed to date; about 12 million sq ft nearing completion.
Sector 71 holds 90-plus acres; about 18 acres is in the RMZ JV, and the branded residence covers 12-plus acres and about 2 million sq ft.
FY26 business development spend about INR7bn for about 2.5 million sq ft in Sohna; FY26 OCF split roughly one-third to BD, similar amount to debt reduction, and balance to approvals and interest.
Launch pipeline over the next 8-12 quarters to monetise the remaining half of the 40 million sq ft.
demand_pricing: Management cites JLL data showing Delhi NCR housing sales up 30% YoY in Q1 2026, and about INR27,000 crore invested in new Gurugram projects in the first four months of 2026.

Price escalation is attributed to a shortage of livable inventory in Gurugram. Management expects normative price increases but says it will not push prices, and FY26 realisation growth was driven by escalation and premium group housing mix.
No mid-rise launches in FY26, so the mix was tilted to premium product.
Launches are expected to achieve about 40% absorption at launch, which is the internal benchmark; management says it has seen this in FY26.
Management flagged global headwinds that could affect the outlook, with no firm view on their impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and location of the INR150bn FY27 launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1: about 2 million sq ft branded residence (Tonino Lamborghini) in Sector 71. Q2-Q3, around Diwali: a similar-sized Sector 71 launch. Q4: the RMZ residential component, plus a 2 million sq ft Southern Peripheral Road parcel later in the year. A smaller Sohna launch (Daxin inventory) and Phase 2 of Sarvam are also planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BD strategy beyond the balance sheet strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on Sohna, where deals are expected to close in H1 FY27, and on larger-format plotted/mixed land parcels for collaborations, following the City of Colours model in Manesar.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY26 collection guidance of INR5,000 crore lower than the INR6,000 crore start-of-year guidance, and why is FY27 not higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers conservative targets; collections and completions are linked, and the company set figures it sees as achievable. Actual FY26 collections were about INR4,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory value on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy ongoing-project inventory is about INR7bn, and recently launched inventory is about INR70-80bn, so total inventory is about INR80-85bn.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 INR15,000 crore launches be sold, and how much of the guidance comes from sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 40% of launch value (about INR6,000 crore) from new launches, with the rest (about INR4,000 crore) from sustenance sales of existing inventory. The analyst's summary of this split was accepted by management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RMZ JV capex and accounting treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a 50-50 JV with equal control. Capex of INR3,500-4,000 crore is expected over 4-4.5 years, funded by JV-level construction debt and equity from both partners. Per Sanjeev Sharma, JV debt stays off the consolidated balance sheet, and equity infusions appear as investment in the JV.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gurugram demand still healthy, and will ticket sizes around INR4 crore per unit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were very few delivered units in Gurugram from 2014-22 and that post-2022 launches have not yet completed, so prices keep rising. It expects about 40%-plus absorption at launch, and said FY27 targets are achievable if the global backdrop stabilises.

risks_watch: Presales fell YoY in FY26; FY27 presales above INR100bn depend on about INR60bn from launches and the timing of the three planned launches in the year.
Completion slippage: FY26 completions were below plan due to monsoon and NGT restrictions, and about 12 million sq ft must finish in 4-5 quarters.
Collections (INR5,000 crore target) were well below the INR6,000 crore FY26 target; FY27 collection of above INR50bn needs execution.
Global macro headwinds were flagged without quantification.
RMZ JV: execution, JV-level debt and equity needs of about INR3,500-4,000 crore, and exceptional-item accounting for the FY26 PAT.
Sohna and plotted BD deals expected in H1 FY27 are not yet closed; FY26 BD was lower than prior years.
543990|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term pipeline and balance sheet, with a deliberately conservative tone on near-term targets. Management was open on the FY26 presales dip and the collections shortfall, and gave specific launch-timing and capex numbers, while giving no firm macro view.
key_quotes: So effectively, we've been formally believing that supply creation leads to demand creation and vice versa.
It's just 2 billion, could have been positive or minus 2, but by and large, this is almost down to a 0 level net debt position.
We are not going to push that sale prices up.
We don't want to kind of get sound very aggressive with regard to these plans.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA margin is 9-10% and gross margin about 30%, with realisation up about 20% YoY to above INR15,000/sq ft from price escalation and premium group housing mix, but management guided no margin number and said it will not push prices.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 12 million sq ft nearing completion over the next 4-5 quarters and about 6.5 million sq ft launched in FY26, with launches of about 2 million sq ft each in Q1, Q2-Q3 and Q4 FY27 (above INR150bn launch value).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 presales guided above INR100bn vs FY26 INR82.5bn (about 20%+ growth, if met), with about 40% sell-through on launch value (about INR60bn) and Delhi NCR housing sales up 30% YoY in Q1 2026 per JLL, though FY26 presales fell from about INR100bn in FY25.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The RMZ JV capex of INR3,500-4,000 crore over 4-4.5 years is already approved, and the land bank is 19 million sq ft with BD deals in Sohna hoped to close in H1 FY27, but no new capex plant is guided and utilisation is not a factor for a developer.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management deliberately set conservative targets (FY26 collections guided at INR5,000 crore vs INR6,000 crore start-of-year, actual about INR4,000 crore), so upgrades are not signalled and FY27 targets are described as achievable only if the global backdrop stabilises.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 presales fell from about INR100bn to INR82.5bn, FY26 completions missed plan due to monsoon and NGT curbs, and about 12 million sq ft must complete in 4-5 quarters to hit INR50bn revenue recognition, with global macro headwinds unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tonino Lamborghini branded residence of about 2 million sq ft is set to launch in Q1 FY27, followed by a similar-sized Sector 71 launch around Diwali (Q2-Q3) and an RMZ residential launch in Q4.

rows.label: FY27 presales above INR100bn
rows.why: Guided above INR100bn vs FY26 INR82.5bn, with about INR60bn from new launches at the 40% absorption benchmark that management says it saw in FY26.

rows.label: RMZ JV activation and Sohna BD deals
rows.why: Sohna and larger-format plotted land deals are expected to close in H1 FY27 against a 19 million sq ft land bank, while the RMZ JV (about 5.5 million sq ft, above INR150bn capital value) is fully licensed with activation planned in FY27.

rows.label: Net debt near zero
rows.why: Net debt has fallen to about INR2bn, a historical low, with FY26 OCF of about INR21bn split roughly one-third to BD and similar amount to debt reduction.

tone.note: Management was confident on the launch pipeline, balance sheet and Gurugram demand, and deliberately conservative on near-term targets; analysts pushed on the FY26 presales dip, the collections shortfall, and whether FY27 targets hold given unquantified global headwinds.

543990|2026-06.headline: Signatureglobal Q1 FY27: pre-sales ~Rs 20bn (20% of Rs 100bn FY target) and collections only Rs 6.7bn, well below the ~Rs 11bn run-rate.
543990|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 2,000 crore, led by the Tonino Lamborghini branded-residence launch in Sector 71, Gurugram, priced above Rs 22,000/sq ft with GDV above Rs 4,000 crore. Realisation across the portfolio rose to over Rs 17,000/sq ft from about Rs 15,000 for FY26. Collections fell to about Rs 6.7bn, which management attributed to lumpy milestone payments slipping into next quarter. Management kept FY27 guidance intact: Rs 150bn of new launches, Rs 100bn of pre-sales, and revenue recognition above Rs 50bn, while signalling a land-buying push inside and outside NCR.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it is in line with the ~Rs 2,000-2,500 crore quarterly run-rate; best quarter last year was Q1 FY26 at ~Rs 2,600 crore
Below the ~Rs 1,100 crore per quarter management cites as its norm
vs a little above Rs 15,000/sq ft for FY26

financial_highlights.value: Under Rs 3.9bn (stated as 'less than Rs. 3.9 billion')
financial_highlights.change: Expected to rise modestly during the year as land buying increases

financial_highlights.metric: Average realisation on Q1 revenue recognised (completed inventory)
financial_highlights.change: Affordable-heavy completions; P&L not reflective of current pricing

segments.name: Residential – Gurugram (Sector 71, Tonino Lamborghini branded residence)
segments.commentary: Over 12 acres, >2 mn sq ft SBA, GDV above Rs 4,000 crore; ~800 units, ~400 opened in Phase 1, 300+ sold. Management has crossed Rs 1,500 crore of sales from this launch.

segments.name: Residential – Sector 71 and SPR (upcoming H2 launches)
segments.commentary: Next launches are planned in SPR, with a good portion of FY27 launches in Sector 71 and some outside the micro-markets.

guidance_outlook: New launches of Rs 150bn for FY27 reaffirmed; further launches planned in Q3 (around Diwali) and Q4.
Pre-sales target of Rs 100bn for FY27 maintained; Q1 delivered about 20% of this.
Revenue recognition of more than Rs 50bn for FY27 and a good PAT from historical projects, with projects worth over Rs 5,000 crore to complete this year.
Collections expected to rise through the year; management says Q2 should be good.
Land capex of roughly Rs 1,500-1,800 crore for FY27 in new business development, in core NCR and outside NCR.
Expects construction cost escalation of 7-8% over a decade, to be budgeted; no sharp spike seen in Q1.
capex_capacity: Delivered about 19 mn sq ft to date; about 9 mn sq ft remains under development, with average completion in 2-3 quarters.
Launched about 23 mn sq ft since Feb 2024 (De Luxe DXP), with GDV of Rs 334bn; sales to date of about Rs 230-240bn.
Forthcoming portfolio of about 17 mn sq ft, including 5 mn sq ft of commercial development with RMZ (announced March); another 12 mn sq ft to launch in FY27 and FY28.
Two large townships, of 125 acres and 140 acres, have been launched in Gurugram.
Land and business development to target large low-rise formats of 100-150 acres in core and new markets; mid-income focus for new markets.
demand_pricing: Delhi NCR H1 2026 launches were 18,470 units (+10% YoY) per Cushman & Wakefield; Gurugram accounted for 74% of luxury launches; average launch price up 24% YoY in Q2 2026.
Management says demand is outpacing supply in Gurugram, and developers are taking inflation-plus price increases.
Management says the Middle East conflict caused a macro headwind during Q1, but the Tonino Lamborghini launch sold well.
Each SPR unit is expected at roughly Rs 5-5.5 crore ticket size.
Management said the sales-to-collections timing is driven by construction milestones, so collections lag sales.

qa_highlights.question: Which geographies are being considered for expansion outside NCR, and what land capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating opportunities and will not name locations yet. Land capex is about Rs 1,500-1,800 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 launches be concentrated in one micro-market, and what are the H2 locations?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of the H2 launches are in SPR, and the third is most likely in SPR too. Some launches will be outside SPR, but Sector 71 holds a large share of the FY27 pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How do branded-residence launches differ, and how fast will they sell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says differentiation comes from product, brand, unit size and orientation. Sales target is about 50% within 3-6 months of launch, with inventory released at about 10% a year until completion. Financial closure comes at around 40% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Why were collections weak, and can they reach Rs 2,000 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 collections were an aberration due to lumpy milestone payments slipping to next quarter. The norm is ~Rs 1,100 crore a quarter, and management expects a good Q2. Sales will convert to collections over time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost trends from geopolitical issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No inordinate material or labour cost increase so far. Long-run escalation of 7-8% is budgeted over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: What product and margin profile will external-market projects have?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-rise, larger-format, mid-income projects are planned to build brand presence and delivery track record in new markets, not small 5-10 acre parcels.

risks_watch: Collections were ~Rs 6.7bn against the ~Rs 11bn norm, so cash conversion depends on slipped milestone payments being received in Q2.
Achieving Rs 100bn pre-sales requires about Rs 80bn over the remaining three quarters, relying on Q3 and launches around Diwali.
Net debt will rise as land buying of Rs 15-18bn is done, against Rs 25bn of cash.
Q1 revenue recognised at under Rs 6,000/sq ft on completed inventory, versus current pricing of Rs 17,000/sq ft; margin mix will shift.
Heavy concentration in Sector 71 and SPR for FY27 launches; new-market entry is still unnamed.
Exposure to Middle East conflict, currency moves and monsoon disruption.
543990|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year targets and on demand, but defensive on the weak collections quarter, which was explained as timing. Evasive on the location of out-of-NCR projects and on pricing for them.
key_quotes: Given our launch pipeline, we stay confident of achieving about Rs. 100 billion of pre-sales for the current year.
Collections, yes, this quarter was a bit of an aberration.
We launched the project at the highest ever price we have achieved ever, which is a little above Rs. 22,000 a foot, hence taking the GDV value in excess of Rs. 4,000 crores

rows.why: Q1 revenue recognised at under Rs 6,000/sq ft on affordable completions vs current realisation above Rs 17,000/sq ft, so P&L mix is not yet reflecting pricing; cost escalation budgeted at 7-8% over a decade with no sharp Q1 spike.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 9 mn sq ft under development with average completion in 2-3 quarters, plus a forthcoming ~17 mn sq ft portfolio with 12 mn sq ft to launch in FY27-FY28 and two townships of 125 and 140 acres already launched.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales of about Rs 20bn in Q1 with launches of Rs 150bn planned for FY27 and about 9 mn sq ft under development; sales target of Rs 100bn for FY27 held.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is raising land buying with Rs 1,500-1,800 crore of FY27 land capex planned in core NCR and outside NCR, and says it is hopeful of adding significant land in core and new markets.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance (Rs 150bn launches, Rs 100bn pre-sales) with Q1 pre-sales at about 20% of the target, requiring about Rs 80bn over three quarters, so no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Pre-sales need about Rs 80bn in the remaining three quarters (~Rs 27bn a quarter vs Rs 20bn in Q1) and collections of Rs 6.7bn were far below the ~Rs 11bn norm, with Q2 collections the test.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (around Diwali) and Q4 FY27
rows.why: Further launches are planned in Q3 and Q4, with SPR units at Rs 5-5.5 crore ticket size and two of the H2 launches in SPR.

rows.label: Collections recovery in Q2 FY27
rows.why: Collections of ~Rs 6.7bn vs ~Rs 11bn norm were attributed to lumpy milestones slipping to next quarter; management expects a good Q2, but this is not yet proven.

rows.label: Net debt rise from land buying
rows.why: Net debt is under Rs 3.9bn against ~Rs 25bn cash, and land buying of Rs 15-18bn is expected to push net debt up modestly during the year.

rows.label: Entry into out-of-NCR markets
rows.why: Management is evaluating locations outside NCR with low-rise, 100-150 acre mid-income formats targeted, but has not named any locations or pricing.

tone.note: Management was confident on full-year targets, Gurugram demand and the Tonino Lamborghini launch, but defensive on the Rs 6.7bn collections quarter and evasive on out-of-NCR locations and pricing.

543992|2026-03.headline: Yatra FY26 revenue less service cost rose 24.5% to INR 4,824 mn and adjusted EBITDA 37.5% to INR 917 mn, but Q4 EBITDA fell 46% on MICE disruption.
543992|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as its most profitable year in company history, with revenue from operations up 27% to INR 10,065 mn and PAT up 28% to INR 468 mn. Q4 was weak: revenue from operations fell 14% YoY to INR 1,890 mn and EBITDA fell 46% to INR 126 mn, driven by West Asia conflict cancellations and deferrals of MICE and international group bookings into FY27. Management said Q1 FY27 run rates are about 20% above Q4 and expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger, while reiterating a medium-term 20% RLSC and 30% adjusted EBITDA CAGR.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue less service cost / gross margin (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY, ahead of revised guidance of 22%
+37.5% YoY, in line with revised guidance

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings (TTV) INR 61,874 mn, up 12% YoY; gross margin INR 2,449 mn, up 30%, with margin rising from 3.42% to 3.96%. Passenger volume was 5,395,000, up 2% for the year; Q4 air passenger volumes grew 9.6% YoY, about 2x industry.

segments.name: Hotels and packages
segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings INR 16,578 mn, up 27%; room nights 1,936,000, up 16%; gross booking margin INR 1,534 mn, up 37%, with margin rising from 8.60% to 9.25%. Standalone hotel margin rose from 7.7% to nearly 9%, and standalone hotels grew about 32% YoY.

segments.name: Corporate / B2E and MICE
segments.commentary: 163 new corporate customers added in FY26 with annual billable value INR 9,568 mn (vs 148 and INR 7,475 mn in FY25). Q4 added 55 clients worth INR 2,709 mn, against 40 worth INR 2,234 mn in Q3. Q4 MICE and international group bookings were cancelled or deferred; retention is about 97%.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Management said B2C is about early 30s% of gross bookings and mid-to-high single-digit operating margin, and is profitable on every transaction.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term CAGR of 20% in revenue less service cost and 30% in adjusted EBITDA reiterated; management said this is not a hard guidance and applies over a 2-3 year horizon.
Q1 FY27 expected to be muted, as about two months of the quarter have already played out; H2 FY27 expected to be materially stronger than H1 on revenge travel and pent-up demand.
Hotel discount-to-gross-margin ratio expected to return to about 75% or lower in H2 FY27 from about 85% in FY26.
ROCE was about 6% in FY26 (about 4% in FY25); management said it would have been 7-7.5% without disruption and targets high-teens ROCE in 3-4 years.
Corporate credit card product expected to be ready to go to market within a quarter or two; hotel virtual card platform already live.
capex_capacity: Migration to Google Cloud and enhanced API infrastructure cited as improving hotel content distribution to domestic and international partners.
Management is investing in MCP protocol integration and agentic-ready platform; announcements expected in FY27, with some innovations 'in a matter of a couple of weeks'.
Expense management product (AI-anchored, launched recently) added 8 logos in Q3 and 8 more in Q4, with 4 live.
Dedicated mid-market corporate sales team set up in Q3 FY26; early contribution seen in Q4.
Corporate wins take 3-6 months to go live and ramp up.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross bookings up 8.3% YoY; total transactions up 16.5-16.6%; hotel room nights up 36%, hotel gross bookings up 9%.
Management attributed the Q4 MICE shortfall to Dubai and Abu Dhabi disruption, higher air fares on Europe MICE, and a 1:3 to 1:3.5 domestic-to-international MICE ticket value ratio.
Hotel average realisation per room night fell on mix shift to affiliate and domestic business away from MICE; management called this short-term.

Air net discount as a share of gross take rose to about 48% in Q4 from about 35% in Q1 FY26 (which management attributed to the Operation Sindoor period); management expects it to near 45% over the next year.
Air gross take rose from 7% in FY24 to 7.1% in FY26 (management's figures); overall gross take about 8.1%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of MICE is international versus domestic, and why was Q4 hit harder than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said international MICE tickets are about 3-3.5x domestic value, and the disruption hit Dubai/Abu Dhabi bookings in March, a peak period. Higher airfares also raised costs on Europe MICE. Q1 FY27 run rate is about 20% above Q4, with growth in Southeast Asia and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to IT services in B2E and AI risk?
qa_highlights.answer: IT services were about 10-11% of B2E business, and about 7% of total B2E including Globe and MICE. The share was about 20% at IPO in FY24.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the air discount rising and what is the take-rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said enterprise customers spend about 50% more per ticket than B2C, so airlines pay better realisation on enterprise. Net take rate is improving. Discount-to-gross-take was about 61% in FY23-24 and about 47-48% in FY25-26.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 tracking better than Q1 FY26, and is the 20% growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20-30 model is a 2-3 year CAGR view, not hard guidance. Q1 will be muted, with recovery expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel realisation and discount trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Discount as share of gross margin was about 75% last year and about 85% in FY26, driven by Q4. Management expects a return to about 75% or lower in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: MICE competition from listed or DRHP-filed MICE companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organised MICE is about 10% of a roughly INR 35,000 crore market, and that Yatra is about the second-largest organised player. It cited exception handling and DMC partnerships as moats. MICE is 10-15% of installed base revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why run B2C at all, and will B2C be split out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2C is self-funding, contribution- and EBITDA-positive, and helps with supplier deals and corporate cross-sell. It declined to segment B2B and B2C formally, but may disclose gross bookings more consistently.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate credit card initiative and its effect on take rate and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Product expected within a quarter or two. Airline partnerships are needed to offset card fees, or the net take rate and numerator would suffer. Hotel virtual card is already live.

qa_highlights.question: Holding company (THCL) restructuring status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Cayman and Cyprus layer collapse is still in progress across India, Cyprus, Singapore and Cayman. THCL sold about 1.8% in Feb 26 to fund legal costs, and management does not expect further sales.

risks_watch: MICE and international group bookings: Q4 cancellations and deferrals; whether deferred business returns in H2 FY27 as management expects.
Hotel realisation and discount-to-gross-margin: Q4 discount rose to about 85% of gross margin; management targets 75% or lower in H2.
Q1 FY27 muted as flagged by management; Middle East conflict and airfare inflation.
Receivable days and working capital; ROCE of about 6% vs high-teens target in 3-4 years.
Corporate credit card rollout: airline fee-sharing needed to protect the net take rate.
Management declined to segment B2B and B2C, and does not disclose advertising revenue separately.
Agentic AI and LLM channels may shift B2C demand; management said the B2E walled-garden model limits exposure.
543992|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long term and cautious on the near term. Management attributed Q4 weakness to conflict-driven MICE and international disruption and called it temporary, but gave no quantified Q1 or FY27 guidance beyond the medium-term 20-30 model. It was evasive on segment disclosure and on the holding company restructuring timeline.

543992|2026-06.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.

Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. 543994|2026-09.headline: JSW Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell 11% to INR328 crore on forex losses and Fujairah's nil contribution.
543994|2026-09.overview: Consolidated operating revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore and operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR674 crore in Q2 FY27. Port EBITDA was flat at INR594 crore, with margin compressing to 49.4% from 53.1%, as Fujairah contributed nothing and coal terminals diluted mix. Logistics EBITDA more than tripled to INR81 crore, with the rail rake fleet raised to 78 from 42. PBT fell to INR431 crore from INR463 crore on unrealised forex losses and higher depreciation, and PAT fell to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Management held the FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore, while revising logistics EBITDA margin guidance up to 28% from 24%.

544004|2026-03.headline: IRM Energy FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 1,066.66 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR 112.25 crore; management guides FY27 volume above 250 MMSCM.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall from Q3 to Q4 FY26?

rows.label: Pre-leasing premium at Max District and Max One

544009|2026-03.headline: Blue Jet FY26 revenue fell 8% to INR947 crores on PI/API destocking, while Q4 contrast media revenue rose 91% YoY to INR193 crores.
544009|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR947 crores, down 8% YoY, with reported EBITDA margin at 31% versus 37% in FY25 as PI/API volumes fell 35%. Contrast media was the offset, growing 23% to INR495 crores for the year and 91% YoY in Q4 to INR193 crores. Management said PI/API destocking is complete and shipments are resuming, and it is ramping investment in Vizag (about INR1,000 crores over roughly 3 years), Mahad Unit 3 and a Hyderabad R&D centre. The company remains debt-free with INR400 crores of liquid assets.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR495 crores (+23%); Q4 INR193 crores (+91% YoY). Flagship product volumes up vs FY25 despite goods in transit; customer FY27 forecast implies mid-single-digit growth for that product. NCE intermediate commercialised in FY25 saw strong FY26 offtake.

segments.name: PI/API (pharma intermediates)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR298 crores (-35%), driven by destocking of a cardiovascular intermediate by an innovator customer. Q4 revenue collapsed to INR2.4 crores from INR40 crores in Q3, with management saying destocking is now complete.

segments.name: Artificial sweetener
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR131 crores (-2%); Q4 INR37 crores (+43% QoQ, -24% YoY). Management cited pricing pressure from imports; one high-volume product is under validation with trial shipments expected over coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Contrast media: management expects double-digit growth in FY27, backed by one or two validations and one commercial launch; molecules include gadolinium and iodinated products. Management declined to quantify.
PI/API: management expects FY27 to exceed the FY25 peak, citing supply-network participation with the innovator customer, but gave no formal guidance.
Margins: management would not guide FY27 margins; Q1 FY27 cost structure to be assessed. Freight costs rose after March 2026 and the FY27 logistics impact is still to be evaluated.
Mahad Unit 3 (backward integration) expected to start production in H2 FY27, with a slow ramp-up.
Hyderabad R&D centre (about INR40 crores) to go live in H2 FY27; product development spend to rise in FY27.

Vizag capacity expected online in 24-30 months; 3-4 contrast media launches and about 2 PI/CDMO opportunities expected to reach commercialisation in FY27.
capex_capacity: Vizag greenfield (about 100 acres): total capex about INR1,000 crores over about 3 years; Phase 1 covers contrast media intermediates, high-intensity sweeteners and pharma intermediates; development activities underway after groundbreaking.
Mahad Unit 3: backward integration project for a key contrast media raw material is progressing; plant expected to go onstream this year.
Mahad facility in final stages of completion; commercial production expected H2 FY27.
Management says contrast media is far from peak utilisation due to ongoing debottlenecking and capacity creation.
Hyderabad R&D centre (about INR40 crores) for peptide intermediates, GLP-1-linked chemistry, biocatalysts and faster CDMO development turnaround.
demand_pricing: PI/API: destocking has happened and the plant is running at optimum capacity; management said the worst is behind for this segment.

Pipeline: about 20 active RFPs in PI/CDMO, mainly chronic therapy areas including GLP-1 and peptide building blocks; 2 expected to commercialise this year. Two high-conviction lateral entries are being evaluated, with dedicated Vizag capacity planned.
Peptides: lab supplies started to some innovators and large peptide CDMOs; management flagged faster price erosion risk in peptides than in contrast media or patented CDMO work.
Artificial sweetener: pricing pressure from imports; management will remain opportunistic.
Raw material costs rose in the last month of FY26 due to the Iran war; rupee depreciation offset this in FY26 and the company is in pass-through discussions with select customers.
Warning letter at one customer's sole formulation plant: management said there is no import alert and no current supply disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence PI will exceed the FY25 peak, and is it confirmed?
qa_highlights.answer: VK Singh said destocking is done, some orders were held back and deferred, and new orders have come in after supply-chain realignment. New products will take time, so little is factored in.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 contrast media revenue is from goods shipped in Q3 (INR190 crores vs INR125 crores in Q3)?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said goods in transit have normalised with no significant variance, so the full INR190 crores belongs to Q4 order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 a step-jump year for contrast media?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiven Arora said the focus is double-digit growth backed by new launches, and declined to say more about a step-jump.

qa_highlights.question: Will Mahad backward integration drive margins or top line?
qa_highlights.answer: VK Singh said the primary aim was supply independence from import price volatility; the two products also open third-party sales, but no numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given freight and crude pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said it is too early to comment and that Q1 FY27 cost structures would be the better guide.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company raising funds, and is it linked to Vizag?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said the situation is dynamic and an update will follow in coming quarters; the company is accelerating capex from its debt-free balance sheet.

risks_watch: FY27 margin pressure from freight and crude-linked raw material costs; management has not quantified the impact.
Contrast media growth depends on FY27 validations and launches, and monthly offtake is uneven; the FY26 Q4 surge may not be repeatable.
Vizag execution: about INR1,000 crores over 3 years, with a 24-30 month window for online capacity; FY27 capex about INR400 crores.

544009|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on contrast media and on PI recovery, but guarded on margins and specifics; management withheld customer, molecule and pricing detail under confidentiality and declined to guide margins until Q1 FY27.

544009|2026-06.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA hit INR98 crore, with PI/API restart offset by INR30 crore contrast media goods in transit.
544009|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR293 crore, up 25% QoQ, with operating EBITDA margin of 33.5% versus 30.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth came mainly from PI and API, where supply of an intermediate restarted after customer destocking. Contrast media revenue fell sharply (about 40% QoQ per analyst) because roughly INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end, which management says will be recognised next quarter. Raw material inflation from March 2026 weighed on gross margin, which fell about 3 points to 53%. Mahad (Unit 3) is now expected to commission later this calendar year, slightly ahead of the earlier H2 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2-3 crore earlier; mainly export incentive and forex gain per management

segments.commentary: Main driver of QoQ growth after restarting supply hit by customer destocking. Management cites a strong order book and visibility for at least the next 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Revenue declined QoQ because about INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end; plant at ~70% utilisation. Management describes the segment as stable with long-term arrangements.

segments.name: High-intensity sweetener
segments.commentary: Stable contributor per management; new sweetener is in pilot validation at the existing facility, with scale-up planned at Vizag.

segments.name: Iodinated contrast media intermediate (ABA-HCL)
segments.commentary: Commercial batches expected to start shortly; positive trend seen by end Q2 or beginning Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Contrast media revenue fell ~40% QoQ; how much revenue is deferred to Q2 and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing goods in transit were about INR30 crore higher than opening, which will be recognised next quarter. Plant utilisation is ~70% steady; production unchanged and production-to-dispatch at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income jump to INR16.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bulk to forex gain and higher interest income, and later clarified the line item is driven mainly by export incentives tied to export levels and byproduct sales; the ratio to exports should remain in a similar range.

qa_highlights.question: Is PI/API growth lumpy or secular, and what visibility exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: secular growth in end-market demand plus a strong order book and consistent production give good visibility for at least 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vizag and cardiovascular-related opportunity translate into sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate, saying it will go by orders on hand; order book described as good and an update to come when more information is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the peptides strategy and differentiation from other Indian CDMOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on peptide fragments first (liquid phase), with selective forward integration into final peptides for large CDMOs or innovators; no participation in generic front-end peptides. Management intends to quantify the peptide-related RFPs in coming quarters.

544012|2026-03.headline: Cello World Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR654 crore (record quarter), but EBITDA margin fell to 20.9%; FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% growth.
544012|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was a record INR653.6 crore, up 11% YoY, with EBITDA of INR136.6 crore (20.9% margin) and PAT of INR90.1 crore (13.8% margin). FY26 revenue grew 8.8% to INR2,323.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR526.4 crore (22.7%) and PAT margin of 14.3%, weighed down by glassware losses and steel bottle ramp-up costs. Management described FY26 as a year of corrective initiatives and said Q1 FY27 looks challenging due to the Middle East-linked cost and demand headwinds. Steel bottle capacity is ramping in phases toward full scale by July 2026, and the Wimplast merger and a restructuring scheme took effect from 27 May 2026.

segments.name: Consumerware
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR434 crore (66.4% of total), up 7% YoY; gross margin 47.8%. Glassware sales grew without profit, and steel ware margins fell 5-6% due to shifting from China sourcing to costlier OEMs. Appliances sold out in March on LPG-driven demand.

segments.name: Writing instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR128 crore (19.6% of total), up 64% YoY including Cello brand from Q4; excluding Cello, grew at a healthy double-digit rate. FY26 segment revenue about INR368 crore; FY27 target INR500 crore plus.

segments.name: Moulded furniture and allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about 14% of total; moulded furniture fell 13.5% YoY in line with industry demand. Wimplast merged into the company; gross margin 39.5%.

segments.commentary: Sales fell 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints, with stock-outs in insulated steel. Two lines running in Q4, four more in Q1 FY27 and two further lines expected soon; peak revenue of current capacity about INR300 crore.

segments.name: Glassware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 60% due to Chinese dumping; segment at breakeven. Management targets peak revenue of about INR300 crore at 28-30% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Opalware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 85%, leaving about 15% headroom; management plans to exhaust capacity before any expansion, which would need a greenfield site in Rajasthan.

FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 2-2.5 percentage points, driven by steel ware and glassware scale-up; consumerware margin improvement of about 2.5-3%.

E-commerce and quick commerce now about 17% of revenue, with profitability in line with other segments.

Glassware faces dumping of imported Chinese products; company is seeking government protection.
Opalware faces new competition about 6-odd months old; management is cautious on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was steel bottle capacity delayed from Q4 FY26 to Q2 FY27, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no delay: lines started in phases, with 2 in Q4, 4 in Q1 FY27 and 2 more after. Steel ware sales fell about 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance for revenue growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 10-12% and EBITDA margin up about 2-2.5 percentage points, with a possible change depending on the crisis.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin compression in consumerware and writing instruments in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Glassware revenue grew without profit, steel ware margin fell 5-6% from costlier OEM sourcing, and appliances carried lower margins. Cello pens were loss-making before the acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top-line guidance conservative given 12-20% MRP hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value growth will come, but volumes could be subdued this year. The price increases may not hold for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash is there and how will it be used? Any buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is being held for adjacent inorganic opportunities with distribution or manufacturing synergies, which may depress return ratios. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to reduce receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to cut 15-odd days to under 100 days, through better channel inventory checks, distributor stock liquidation support and SKU rationalisation. Government tenders stretched receivables.

Glassware remains at about 60% utilisation and breakeven under Chinese dumping; protection outcome pending.
Steel bottle ramp-up to full scale by July 2026 is a key execution milestone.

Receivable days stretched by government tenders; target 15-odd days reduction.
Surplus cash and low return ratios; any inorganic deal would be a capital allocation test.

Asset quality improved: GNPA fell to 5.4% from 6.9% and NNPA to 1.8% from 3.0% YoY, with Q4 slippages of INR 106 crore versus INR 427 crore a year earlier. Management framed FY26 as two halves, with the second half showing improvement from secured-asset mix shift, collections and cost discipline. Management guided to steady-state credit cost of about 2% from FY28, steady-state ROA of 2%, and NIM of about 7%, while noting provisioning backlog will persist in FY27.
